title.en: Volume 89 Biographies 14: Qu, Shi, Wei, Chi, Zhang, Qin, Tang, Duan
title.raw: 卷八十九 列傳第十四 屈實尉遲張秦唐段 Volume 89 Biographies 14: Qu, Shi, Wei, Chi, Zhang, Qin, Tang, Duan

sentences.zh: 屈突通，其先蓋昌黎徒何人，後家長安。

translations.literal: Qu Tutong: his ancestors were probably Tuohe people of Changli; later the family settled in Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: Qu Tutong came of a clan said to be Tuohe people from Changli, and later made their home in Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 仕隋爲虎賁郎將。

translations.literal: He served the Sui as a Tiger Guard commandant.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Sui he held the post of Tiger Guard commandant.

sentences.zh: 文帝命覆隴西牧簿，得隱馬二萬匹，帝怒州龍門（今山西河津）人。

translations.literal: Emperor Wen ordered a review of the Longxi pasture records; twenty thousand hidden horses were found. The Emperor was furious—[the scandal touched] Longmen prefecture (modern Hejin, Shanxi).
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wen ordered an audit of the Longxi pasture books and uncovered twenty thousand concealed horses, his wrath fell on the officials—many tied to Longmen (in present-day Hejin, Shanxi).

sentences.zh: 曾於河、汾之間授徒千人，時稱，收太僕卿慕容悉達、監牧官史千五百人，將悉殊死。

translations.literal: He had once taught a thousand disciples between the Yellow and Fen Rivers and was famed for it; [the court] arrested Grand Master of the Stud Murong Xida and fifteen hundred pasture officials, intending to execute them all.
translations.idiomatic: Renowned as a teacher of a thousand students along the Yellow and Fen, he now saw the court seize Murong Xida, Grand Master of the Stud, and fifteen hundred pasture officials, all marked for death.

sentences.zh: 通曰：「人命至重，死不復生。

translations.literal: Tutong said: "Human life is supremely weighty; once dead it does not return to life.
translations.idiomatic: Tutong said, "A human life outweighs everything—death cannot be undone.

sentences.zh: 陛下以至仁育四海，豈容以畜產一日而戮千五百士？」

translations.literal: Your Majesty nurtures the four seas with utmost benevolence—how could you allow livestock in a single day to bring the execution of fifteen hundred men?"
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty rules the realm with supreme humanity—how can livestock justify slaughtering fifteen hundred men in a day?"

sentences.zh: 帝叱之，通進頓首曰：「臣願身就戮，以延眾死。」

translations.literal: The Emperor shouted at him. Tutong advanced, knocked his head to the ground, and said: "This subject is willing to accept execution himself in order to spare the multitude from death."
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor rebuked him. Tutong stepped forward, prostrated himself, and said, "Let me die in their place—spare these men."

sentences.zh: 帝寤，曰：「朕不明，乃至是。

translations.literal: The Emperor came to his senses and said: "I have been unenlightened, to have come to this.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor woke to himself and said, "My judgment failed me to bring matters so far.

sentences.zh: 今當免悉達等，旌爾善言。」

translations.literal: Now Xida and the others shall be pardoned, to honor your good words."
translations.idiomatic: Xida and the rest shall be spared—your counsel deserves reward."

sentences.zh: 遂皆以減論。

translations.literal: Thereupon all were sentenced by reduction [of penalty].
translations.idiomatic: In the end all received reduced sentences instead of death.

sentences.zh: 擢左武衛將軍。

translations.literal: He was promoted to General of the Left Martial Guard.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to general of the Left Martial Guard.

sentences.zh: 蒞官勁正，有犯法者，雖親無所回縱。

translations.literal: In office he was stern and upright; when anyone violated the law, even kin received no leniency.
translations.idiomatic: He governed with iron rectitude: kin or stranger, the lawbreaker found no favor.

sentences.zh: 其弟蓋爲長安令，亦以方嚴顯。

translations.literal: His younger brother Gai was magistrate of Chang'an and likewise won fame for severity.
translations.idiomatic: His brother Gai, magistrate of Chang'an, was equally famed for uncompromising rule.

sentences.zh: 時爲語曰：「寧食三斗艾，不見屈突蓋；

translations.literal: At the time people said in verse: "Better eat three dou of mugwort than meet Qu Tutu Gai;
translations.idiomatic: A saying ran: "Better swallow three pecks of wormwood than face Qu Tutu Gai;

sentences.zh: 寧食三斗蔥，不逢屈突通。」

translations.literal: better eat three dou of scallions than encounter Qu Tutong."
translations.idiomatic: better choke down three pecks of scallions than cross Qu Tutong."

sentences.zh: 煬帝即位，遣持詔召漢王諒。

translations.literal: When Emperor Yang acceded, he dispatched Tutong bearing an edict to summon Prince Liang of Han.
translations.idiomatic: On Yang's accession he sent Tutong with an imperial summons for Prince Liang of Han.

sentences.zh: 先是，文帝與諒約，若璽書召，驗視敕字加點，又與玉麟符合，則就道。

translations.literal: Earlier, Emperor Wen and Liang had agreed: if a sealed summons came, one must verify an added dot beside the edict character and a jade tally of matching form—only then set out.
translations.idiomatic: Wen and Liang had agreed on a secret sign: a dot beside the edict character and a matching jade tally would prove a genuine summons.

sentences.zh: 及是，書無驗，諒覺變，詰通，通占對無屈，竟得歸長安。

translations.literal: When this arrived the document bore no verification; Liang sensed treachery and questioned Tutong. Tutong answered with unbending composure and at last returned to Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: The letter lacked the signs; Liang smelled a trap and pressed Tutong, who answered without faltering and eventually made his way back to Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 大業中，與宇文述共破楊玄感，以功遷左驍衛大將軍。

translations.literal: In the Daye era he joined Yuwen Shu to crush Yang Xuangan and, for merit, was transferred to Grand General of the Left Valiant Cavalry Guard.
translations.idiomatic: During Daye he and Yuwen Shu defeated Yang Xuangan; for that service he became grand general of the Left Valiant Cavalry Guard.

sentences.zh: 秦、隴盜起，授關內討捕大使。

translations.literal: When bandits rose in Qin and Long, he was appointed Grand Commissioner for Suppression and Capture within the Passes.
translations.idiomatic: As Qin and Long erupted in rebellion he was named grand commissioner to hunt bandits inside the passes.

sentences.zh: 安定人劉迦論反，眾十餘萬據雕陰。

translations.literal: Liu Jialun of Anding rebelled; a host of more than a hundred thousand held Diaoyin.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Jialun of Anding rose with an army of a hundred thousand and seized Diaoyin.

sentences.zh: 通發關中兵擊之，次安定，初不與戰，軍中意其怯。

translations.literal: Tutong mobilized Guanzhong troops to strike him, halted at Anding, and at first would not give battle; the army thought him timid.
translations.idiomatic: Tutong marched Guanzhong troops against him and camped at Anding without fighting; his men took this for cowardice.

sentences.zh: 通陽言旋師，而潛入上郡。

translations.literal: Tutong openly announced withdrawal but secretly entered Shang commandery.
translations.idiomatic: He proclaimed a withdrawal while slipping secretly into Shang commandery.

sentences.zh: 賊未之覺，引而南，去通七十里舍，分兵徇地。

translations.literal: The rebels did not perceive it; they drew south, encamped seventy li from Tutong, and divided forces to raid the countryside.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels never noticed; they marched south, pitched camp seventy li from Tutong, and sent detachments to plunder the land.

sentences.zh: 通候其無備，夜簡精甲襲破之，斬迦論並首級萬餘，築京觀於上郡南山，虜老弱數萬口。

translations.literal: Tutong waited until they were unguarded, chose elite armor by night, and stormed them to ruin; he beheaded Jialun and more than ten thousand heads, built a victory mound on the southern hill of Shang, and took captive old and weak numbering tens of thousands.
translations.idiomatic: When their guard dropped, Tutong picked elite troops and struck by night, killing Jialun and ten thousand more, raising a victory mound on Shang's southern hill, and carrying off tens of thousands of noncombatants.

sentences.zh: 後隋政益亂，盜賊多，士無鬥志，諸將多覆。

translations.literal: Later Sui rule grew ever more chaotic; bandits multiplied, soldiers lost fighting spirit, and many generals were destroyed.
translations.idiomatic: As the Sui order crumbled, bandits swarmed, troops lost heart, and commanders fell one after another.

sentences.zh: 通每向必持重，雖不大克，亦不敗負。

translations.literal: Whenever Tutong took the field he was deliberate; though he did not win great victories, he also did not suffer defeat.
translations.idiomatic: Tutong campaigned with caution: few sweeping triumphs, but never a rout.

sentences.zh: 帝南幸，使鎮長安。

translations.literal: When the Emperor toured south, he left Tutong to garrison Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor traveled south on tour, Tutong was left to hold Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 高祖起，代王遣通守河東，戰久不下，高祖留兵圍之，遂濟河，破其將桑顯和於飲馬泉。

translations.literal: When Gaozu rose, the Prince of Dai sent Tutong to hold Hedong; battle dragged without capture. Gaozu left troops to besiege it, crossed the river, and defeated his general Sang Xianhe at Drinking-Horse Spring.
translations.idiomatic: After Gaozu's uprising the Prince of Dai posted Tutong in Hedong; the siege stalled until Gaozu crossed the Yellow River and shattered Sang Xianhe at Drinking-Horse Spring.

sentences.zh: 通大懼，乃留鷹揚郎將堯君素守蒲，將自武關趨藍田以援長安。

translations.literal: Tutong was greatly afraid; he left Eagle-Banner commandant Yao Junsu to hold Pu and intended to hurry through Wu Pass toward Lantian to relieve Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: In panic Tutong left Yao Junsu to hold Pu and marched for Wu Pass and Lantian to save Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 至潼關，阻劉文靜兵不得進，相持月餘。

translations.literal: Reaching Tong Pass he was blocked by Liu Wenjing's troops and could not advance; they faced each other for more than a month.
translations.idiomatic: At Tong Pass Liu Wenjing barred his way; the two armies glared at each other for over a month.

sentences.zh: 通令顯和夜襲文靜，詰朝大戰，顯和縱兵破二壁，唯文靜一壁獨完，然數入壁，短兵接，文靜中流矢，軍垂敗，顯和以士疲，乃傳餐食，文靜因得分兵實二壁。

translations.literal: Tutong ordered Xianhe to raid Wenjing by night; at dawn came great battle. Xianhe loosed his troops and broke two ramparts; only Wenjing's one rampart remained intact, yet he entered the rampart repeatedly in close combat. Wenjing took a stray arrow; the army neared collapse. Xianhe, seeing the men exhausted, called for food to be passed along; Wenjing thereby could divide troops to fill the two ramparts.
translations.idiomatic: Tutong sent Xianhe to strike Wenjing by night; at dawn the fight raged. Xianhe smashed two walls, but Wenjing's third held as men grappled hand to hand. Wenjing was wounded, his line buckling—until Xianhe paused to feed his weary troops, giving Wenjing time to reinforce the broken walls.

sentences.zh: 會遊軍數百騎自南山還，擊其背，三壁兵大呼，奮而出，顯和遂潰，盡得其眾。

translations.literal: Just then several hundred mounted scouts returning from the southern hills struck their rear; troops at all three ramparts shouted and charged out with spirit. Xianhe collapsed; they took his entire force.
translations.idiomatic: Then hundreds of Tang scouts swept down from the southern hills onto the Sui rear; all three walls erupted in a shout and charge. Xianhe's army broke and was taken whole.

sentences.zh: 通勢蹙，或說之降，曰：「吾蒙國厚恩，事二主，安可逃難？

translations.literal: Tutong's situation tightened; some urged surrender. He said: "I have received the state's deep grace and served two sovereigns—how could I flee hardship?
translations.idiomatic: Cornered, Tutong was urged to yield. He said, "The state heaped favor on me; I served two emperors—how could I run from this ordeal?

sentences.zh: 獨有死報爾！」

translations.literal: There is only repaying with death!"
translations.idiomatic: I owe nothing but a death in its service!"

sentences.zh: 每自摩其頸曰：「要當爲國家受人一刀！」

translations.literal: He would stroke his own neck and say: "I must yet take a blade for the state!"
translations.idiomatic: He would rub his neck and say, "Soon enough the state will have my neck for the blade."

sentences.zh: 其訓勉士卒必流涕，故力雖窮，而人尚爲之感奮。

translations.literal: When he exhorted the soldiers he always wept; though strength was spent, men were still stirred by him.
translations.idiomatic: His exhortations always ended in tears, and though their strength was spent the men still rallied to him.

sentences.zh: 帝遣其家僮往召，通趨斬之。

translations.literal: The Emperor sent a household servant to summon him; Tutong rushed forward and beheaded the man.
translations.idiomatic: The Sui emperor sent a household slave to recall him; Tutong had the messenger cut down.

sentences.zh: 俄聞京師平，家盡沒，乃留顯和保潼關，率兵將如洛。

translations.literal: Soon he heard the capital had fallen and his household was wholly lost; he left Xianhe to hold Tong Pass and led troops intending toward Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: Word came that the capital had fallen and his family was gone; he left Xianhe at Tong Pass and marched east toward Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 既行，而顯和來降。

translations.literal: Once he had marched, Xianhe came over in surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Hardly had he left when Xianhe surrendered to the Tang.

sentences.zh: 文靜遣竇琮、段志玄精騎追及於稠桑，通結陣拒之。

translations.literal: Wenjing sent Dou Cong and Duan Zhixuan with elite cavalry to overtake him at Chousang; Tutong formed battle lines to resist.
translations.idiomatic: Wenjing sent Dou Cong and Duan Zhixuan in pursuit; at Chousang Tutong turned to fight.

sentences.zh: 琮縱其子壽往諭使降，通大呼曰：「昔與汝父子，今則仇也！」

translations.literal: Cong sent his son Shou to persuade surrender. Tutong shouted: "Once we were father and son—now we are foes!"
translations.idiomatic: Cong let his son Shou approach to parley. Tutong roared, "We were kin once—now we are enemies!"

sentences.zh: 命左右射之，顯和呼其眾曰：「京師陷，諸君皆家關西，何爲復東？」

translations.literal: He ordered attendants to shoot. Xianhe called to the troops: "The capital has fallen; you all have homes in Guanxi—why march east again?"
translations.idiomatic: He ordered arrows loosed. Xianhe shouted to the ranks, "The capital is lost and your homes lie west—why follow this road east?"

sentences.zh: 眾皆舍兵。

translations.literal: The multitude all cast down their weapons.
translations.idiomatic: The soldiers dropped their arms.

sentences.zh: 通知不免，遂下馬東南向，再拜號哭曰：「臣力屈兵敗，不負陛下。」

translations.literal: Knowing he could not escape, Tutong dismounted facing southeast, bowed twice, and wailed: "This subject's strength is spent and his army defeated, yet he has not failed Your Majesty."
translations.idiomatic: Seeing capture inevitable, Tutong dismounted toward the southeast, kowtowed, and wept, "My force is broken, but I have not betrayed Your Majesty."

sentences.zh: 遂被禽，送長安。

translations.literal: He was then taken captive and sent to Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: They seized him and brought him to Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 帝勞曰：「何相見晚邪？」

translations.literal: The Emperor comforted him: "Why did we meet so late?"
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu greeted him warmly: "Why did we wait so long to meet?"

sentences.zh: 泣曰：「通不能盡人臣之節，故至此，爲本朝羞。」

translations.literal: He wept and said: "Tutong could not fulfill a minister's duty, and so came to this—shame to our dynasty."
translations.idiomatic: Tutong wept, "I could not keep faith as a subject of the Sui—this end shames the house I served."

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「忠臣也！」

translations.literal: The Emperor said: "A loyal minister!"
translations.idiomatic: "A true loyalist," said the Emperor."

sentences.zh: 釋之，授兵部尚書、蔣國公，爲秦王行軍元帥長史。

translations.literal: He released him, appointed him Minister of War and Duke of Jiang, and made him chief clerk to the Prince of Qin's campaigning marshal.
translations.idiomatic: He freed him, named him Minister of War and Duke of Jiang, and attached him to the Prince of Qin as marshal's chief clerk.

sentences.zh: 從平薛仁杲，時賊珍用山積，諸將爭得之，通獨無所取。

translations.literal: He followed in pacifying Xue Rengao; at the time rebel treasures piled like hills and generals scrambled for them—Tutong alone took nothing.
translations.idiomatic: In the campaign against Xue Rengao, loot heaped mountain-high while every general grabbed his share—Tutong took nothing.

sentences.zh: 帝聞，曰：「清以奉國，名定不虛。」

translations.literal: The Emperor heard and said: "Integrity in service to the state—his reputation is surely not empty."
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor said on hearing it, "He serves the state with clean hands—his name is earned."

sentences.zh: 特賚金銀六百兩、彩千段。

translations.literal: He specially bestowed six hundred taels of gold and silver and a thousand bolts of brocade.
translations.idiomatic: He rewarded him with six hundred taels of gold and silver and a thousand bolts of silk.

sentences.zh: 判陜東道行臺左僕射，從討王世充。

translations.literal: He served as acting Left Vice-President of the Shandong Circuit headquarters and followed in the campaign against Wang Shichong.
translations.idiomatic: As acting left vice-president of the eastern-Shanxi headquarters he joined the war on Wang Shichong.

sentences.zh: 時通二子在洛，帝曰：「今以東略屬公，如二子何？」

translations.literal: At the time Tutong's two sons were in Luoyang. The Emperor said: "The eastern campaign is now entrusted to you—what of your two sons?"
translations.idiomatic: Tutong's two sons were still in Luoyang. The Emperor asked, "I give you the eastern front—what of your boys?"

sentences.zh: 通曰：「臣老矣，不足當重任。

translations.literal: Tutong said: "Your subject is old and not equal to a weighty charge.
translations.idiomatic: Tutong replied, "I am too old for so great a trust.

sentences.zh: 然疇昔陛下釋俘累，加恩禮，以蒙更生，是時口與心誓，以死許國。

translations.literal: Yet in former days Your Majesty released this captive, heaped grace and ceremony, and granted renewed life; then mouth and heart swore together to pledge death to the state.
translations.idiomatic: Yet when Your Majesty spared my life and honored me, I swore in heart and voice to repay the state with my death.

sentences.zh: 今日之行，正當先驅，二兒死自其分，終不以私害義。」

translations.literal: Today's march should rightly be as vanguard; if the two sons die, that is their allotted portion—I will never let private feeling harm righteousness."
translations.idiomatic: Today I should ride in the van; if my sons die, so be it—I will not let kinship stain duty."

sentences.zh: 帝太息曰：「烈士徇節，吾今見之。」

translations.literal: The Emperor sighed deeply: "A man of fervor dying for principle—I see it today."
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor sighed, "A man who would die for principle—I have seen one at last."

sentences.zh: 及竇建德來援賊，秦王分麾下半以屬通，俾與齊王圍洛。

translations.literal: When Dou Jiande came to aid the rebel, the Prince of Qin gave half his command to Tutong and had him with the Prince of Qi besiege Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: When Dou Jiande marched to relieve Wang Shichong, the Prince of Qin gave Tutong half the army to hold the siege with Prince Qi.

sentences.zh: 世充平，論功第一，拜陜東道大行臺右僕射，鎮東都。

translations.literal: When Shichong was pacified, in merit reckoning he ranked first; he was appointed Right Vice-President of the great Shandong headquarters and garrisoned the eastern capital.
translations.idiomatic: After Shichong fell Tutong's merit ranked first; he became right vice-president of the eastern headquarters and governor of the eastern capital.

sentences.zh: 數歲，召爲刑部尚書。

translations.literal: After several years he was summoned as Minister of Punishments.
translations.idiomatic: Some years later he was recalled as Minister of Punishments.

sentences.zh: 自以不習文，固辭，改工部。

translations.literal: Considering himself unversed in letters, he firmly declined and was shifted to the Ministry of Works.
translations.idiomatic: Claiming no skill in law, he refused firmly and was moved to the Ministry of Works.

sentences.zh: 建成之變，復檢校行臺僕射，馳鎮洛。

translations.literal: At the Jian Cheng incident he was again made acting headquarters vice-president and galloped to garrison Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: After the Xuanwu Gate crisis he was again named acting headquarters vice-president and rushed to secure Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 貞觀初，行臺廢，爲洛州都督，進左光祿大夫。

translations.literal: Early in Zhenguan the headquarters was abolished; he became military governor of Luozhou and advanced to Left Grand Master of Splendid Happiness.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Zhenguan the regional headquarters was dissolved; he became governor of Luozhou and grand master of splendid happiness.

sentences.zh: 卒，年七十二，贈尚書左僕射，謚曰忠。

translations.literal: He died at seventy-two; posthumously honored as Left Vice-President of the Secretariat, posthumous title Loyal.
translations.idiomatic: He died at seventy-two, posthumously made left vice-president of the Secretariat with the title Loyal.

sentences.zh: 後詔配饗太宗廟廷。

translations.literal: Later an edict paired him in sacrifice at Taizong's temple court.
translations.idiomatic: Later he was granted co-sacrifice in Taizong's ancestral temple.

sentences.zh: 永徽中，贈司空。

translations.literal: In the Yonghui era he was posthumously made Minister of Works [rank].
translations.idiomatic: Under Yonghui he was posthumously elevated to minister of works.

sentences.zh: 二子壽、詮，壽襲爵。

translations.literal: His two sons were Shou and Quan; Shou inherited the title.
translations.idiomatic: He had two sons, Shou and Quan; Shou succeeded to the dukedom.

sentences.zh: 太宗幸洛，思通忠節，故詮以少子拜果毅都尉，賜粟帛恤其家，終瀛州刺史。

translations.literal: When Taizong visited Luoyang and recalled Tutong's loyal integrity, he therefore appointed Quan, as younger son, colonel of the resolute cavalry, granted grain and cloth to comfort the household, and he ended as prefect of Yingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: On a visit to Luoyang Taizong remembered Tutong's fidelity and made the younger son Quan a colonel of resolute cavalry, sending grain and cloth to the family; Quan later died as prefect of Yingzhou.

sentences.zh: 詮子仲翔，神龍中，復守瀛州。

translations.literal: Quan's son Zhongxiang, in the Shenlong era, again held Yingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Quan's son Zhongxiang served again as prefect of Yingzhou in the Shenlong period.

sentences.zh: 初，桂州都督李弘節亦以清慎顯。

translations.literal: Earlier, Li Hongjie, military governor of Guizhou, had also been famed for purity and caution.
translations.idiomatic: Li Hongjie of Guizhou had likewise been known for scrupulous integrity.

sentences.zh: 既歿，其家賣珠。

translations.literal: After his death his household sold pearls.
translations.idiomatic: After he died his family sold pearls to live.

sentences.zh: 太宗疑弘節實貪，欲追坐舉者。

translations.literal: Taizong suspected Hongjie had truly been greedy and wished to punish those who had recommended him.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong suspected Hongjie had been corrupt after all and meant to punish his sponsors.

sentences.zh: 魏徵曰：「陛下過矣！

translations.literal: Wei Zheng said: "Your Majesty goes too far!
translations.idiomatic: Wei Zheng said, "Your Majesty mistakes the matter!

sentences.zh: 且今號清白死不變者，屈突通、張道源。

translations.literal: Moreover, those now called pure in life and unchanging in death are Qu Tutong and Zhang Daoyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Men famed for spotless lives who never bent even in death are Qu Tutong and Zhang Daoyuan.

sentences.zh: 通二子來調，共一馬；

translations.literal: Tutong's two sons came on assignment sharing one horse;
translations.idiomatic: Tutong's sons arrived on court business sharing a single mount;

sentences.zh: 道源子不能自存。

translations.literal: Daoyuan's son could not support himself.
translations.idiomatic: Daoyuan's son could barely keep himself alive.

sentences.zh: 審其清者不加恤，疑其濁者罪所舉，亦好善不篤矣。」

translations.literal: to confirm the pure yet grant no relief, while those suspected of corruption punish their recommenders—this too is not steadfast in cherishing goodness."
translations.idiomatic: yet you comfort no proven upright man while punishing the patrons of the suspect—how is that steadfast love of virtue?"

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「朕未之思。」

translations.literal: The Emperor said: "We had not considered this."
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor said, "I had not thought it through."

sentences.zh: 置不問。

translations.literal: He set the matter aside without inquiry.
translations.idiomatic: He dropped the case.

sentences.zh: 故通之清益顯云。

translations.literal: Thus Tutong's purity shone all the more.
translations.idiomatic: And so Tutong's integrity stood out the brighter.

sentences.zh: 尉遲恭尉遲敬德，名恭，以字行，朔州善陽人。

translations.literal: Yuchi Gong—Yuchi Jingde: his name was Gong, but he went by his style; a man of Shanyang in Shuozhou.
translations.idiomatic: Yuchi Jingde (courtesy name Gong, by which he was commonly known) came from Shanyang in Shuozhou.

sentences.zh: 隋大業末，從軍高陽，積閲爲朝散大夫。

translations.literal: Late in Sui Daye he followed the army at Gaoyang and, through accumulated review, became Grand Master of Palace Leisure.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of Daye he soldiered at Gaoyang and rose by seniority to grand master of palace leisure.

sentences.zh: 劉武周亂，以爲偏將。

translations.literal: When Liu Wuzhou rebelled, he was made a flank general.
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Wuzhou rose in rebellion he served as a flank general.

sentences.zh: 與宋金剛南侵，得晉、澮等州，襲破永安王孝基，執獨孤懷恩等。

translations.literal: With Song Jingang he invaded south, took Jin, Fen, and other prefectures, stormed and broke Prince Xiaoji of Yong'an, and seized Dugu Huai'en and others.
translations.idiomatic: He marched south with Song Jingang, seized Jin and Fen, routed Prince Xiaoji of Yong'an, and captured Dugu Huai'en.

sentences.zh: 武德二年，秦王戰柏壁，金剛敗奔突厥，敬德合余眾守介休，王遣任城王道宗、宇文士及諭之，乃與尋相舉地降，引爲右一府統軍，從擊王世充。

translations.literal: In Wude year two the Prince of Qin fought at Baiyu; Jingang was defeated and fled to the Turks. Jingde gathered the remaining host to hold Jiexiu. The Prince sent Prince Daozong of Ren City and Yuwen Shiji to persuade him; then with Xun Xiang he surrendered the territory, was brought in as commander of the Right First Office, and followed in attacking Wang Shichong.
translations.idiomatic: In Wude 2 the Prince of Qin fought at Baiyu; Jingang fled to the Turks while Jingde held Jiexiu with the remnants. After envoys from Daozong and Yuwen Shiji, he and Xun Xiang surrendered; the Prince made him commander of the right first guard and took him against Wang Shichong.

sentences.zh: 會尋相叛，諸將疑敬德且亂，囚之。

translations.literal: When Xun Xiang rebelled, the generals suspected Jingde would also revolt and imprisoned him.
translations.idiomatic: Xun Xiang's defection made the generals fear Jingde would follow; they threw him in chains.

sentences.zh: 行臺左僕射屈突通、尚書殷開山曰：「敬德慓敢，今執之，猜貳已結，不即殺，後悔無及也。」

translations.literal: Left Vice-President of the headquarters Qu Tutong and Minister Yin Kaishan said: "Jingde is fierce and bold; now that he is seized, suspicion is already fixed—if he is not killed at once, regret will come too late."
translations.idiomatic: Qu Tutong and Yin Kaishan urged, "Jingde is dangerous—suspicion is already sown. Kill him now or regret it forever."

sentences.zh: 王曰：「不然。

translations.literal: The Prince said: "Not so.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince said, "No.

sentences.zh: 敬德必叛，寧肯後尋相者邪？」

translations.literal: If Jingde were sure to rebel, would he lag behind Xun Xiang?"
translations.idiomatic: If he meant to rebel, would he have waited for Xun Xiang?"

sentences.zh: 釋之，引見臥內，曰：「丈夫以氣相許，小嫌不足置胸中，我終不以讒害良士。」

translations.literal: He released him, received him in the inner chamber, and said: "Men pledge by spirit; small grievances are not worth lodging in the breast—I will never let slander harm a good man."
translations.idiomatic: He freed him and received him privately: "Men swear by honor; petty slights do not stay in my heart, and I will not let gossip ruin a worthy man."

sentences.zh: 因賜之金，曰：「必欲去，以爲汝資。」

translations.literal: He then gave him gold, saying: "If you must leave, take this as your provision."
translations.idiomatic: He gave him gold: "If you must go, let this fund your way."

sentences.zh: 是日獵榆窠，會世充自將兵數萬來戰，單雄信者，賊驍將也，騎直趨王，敬德躍馬大呼橫刺，雄信墜，乃翼王出，率兵還戰，大敗之，禽其將陳智略，獲排槊兵六千。

translations.literal: That day they hunted at Elm Hollow; Shichong himself led tens of thousands to battle. Shan Xiongxin was a fierce rebel general whose horse charged straight at the Prince. Jingde leapt his mount, shouted, and thrust across—Xiongxin fell. He then shielded the Prince out, led troops back to fight, and routed them utterly, capturing the general Chen Zhilüe and taking six thousand pike-soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: That day at Elm Hollow hunt, Shichong attacked with tens of thousands. Rebel champion Shan Xiongxin charged the Prince; Jingde spurred forward, shouted, and unhorsed him, shielded the Prince clear, wheeled back, smashed the enemy, took Chen Zhilüe, and six thousand pike troops.

sentences.zh: 王顧曰：「比眾人意公必叛，我獨保無它，何相報速邪？」

translations.literal: The Prince looked back and said: "Just now everyone thought you would surely rebel; I alone held you blameless—why repay so swiftly?"
translations.idiomatic: The Prince said, "All expected you to turn traitor; I alone trusted you—how swift your answer!"

sentences.zh: 賜金銀一篋。

translations.literal: He bestowed a casket of gold and silver.
translations.idiomatic: He gave him a chest of gold and silver.

sentences.zh: 竇建德營板渚，王命李勣等爲伏，親挾弓，令敬德執槊，略其壘，大呼致師。

translations.literal: Dou Jiande encamped at Banzhu; the Prince ordered Li Jing and others as ambush, himself strung the bow, had Jingde bear the pike, skirmished their ramparts, and shouted to bring on battle.
translations.idiomatic: At Banzhu the Prince hid Li Jing in ambush, strung his own bow, put a pike in Jingde's hands, probed Jiande's lines, and shouted the enemy forward.

sentences.zh: 建德兵出，乃稍引卻，殺數十人，眾益進。

translations.literal: Jiande's troops came out; he then drew back slightly, killed several tens, and the host pressed ever forward.
translations.idiomatic: Jiande's men poured out; the Prince feigned retreat, cut down dozens, and drew them deeper in.

sentences.zh: 伏發，大破之。

translations.literal: The ambush struck; they were utterly broken.
translations.idiomatic: The ambush rose and shattered them.

sentences.zh: 時世充兄子琬使於建德，乘隋帝廄馬，鎧甲華整，出入軍中以誇眾。

translations.literal: At the time Shichong's nephew Wan was envoy to Jiande, riding the Sui emperor's stable horse with splendid armor, passing through the army to awe the crowd.
translations.idiomatic: Shichong's nephew Wan rode the Sui emperor's stallion in gleaming armor through Jiande's camp to impress the troops.

sentences.zh: 王望見，問「誰可取者？」

translations.literal: The Prince saw him from afar and asked, "Who can take him?"
translations.idiomatic: The Prince spotted him and asked, "Who can seize him?"

sentences.zh: 敬德請與高甑生、梁建方三騎馳往，禽琬，引其馬以歸，賊不敢動。

translations.literal: Jingde asked to go with Gao Zaosheng and Liang Jianfang—three riders galloping forth, seizing Wan and leading his horse back; the rebels did not dare stir.
translations.idiomatic: Jingde, Gao Zaosheng, and Liang Jianfang galloped out, captured Wan and his horse, and returned while the enemy froze.

sentences.zh: 從討劉黑闥，賊以奇兵襲李勣，王勒兵掩其後，俄而賊眾四面合，敬德率壯士馳入賊，王乘陣亂乃得出。

translations.literal: He followed in campaigning against Liu Heita; rebels with odd troops struck Li Jing. The Prince drove troops to cover their rear; soon rebel masses closed from four sides. Jingde led stalwarts charging into the enemy; the Prince rode the chaos of the lines and only then got out.
translations.idiomatic: Against Liu Heita, rebel raiders hit Li Jing; the Prince swung to their rear, but the ring closed. Jingde plunged in with picked men while the Prince broke free in the confusion.

sentences.zh: 又破徐圓朗。

translations.literal: He again defeated Xu Yuanlang.
translations.idiomatic: He helped crush Xu Yuanlang as well.

sentences.zh: 以功授王府左二副護軍。

translations.literal: For merit he was appointed deputy protector-general of the Prince's Left Second Office.
translations.idiomatic: For these deeds he became deputy protector of the prince's left second guard.

sentences.zh: 隱太子嘗以書招之，贈金皿一車。

translations.literal: The Hidden Crown Prince once recruited him by letter and gave a cartload of gold vessels.
translations.idiomatic: Crown Prince Li Jiancheng once wooed him by letter with a cartload of gold plate.

sentences.zh: 辭曰：「敬德起幽賤，會天下喪亂，久陷逆地，秦王實生之，方以身徇恩。

translations.literal: He declined, saying: "Jingde rose from obscurity and low station; he met the world's ruin and long lay in rebel lands—the Prince of Qin truly gave him life, and he is just now ready to give body for grace.
translations.idiomatic: He refused: "I was nobody until chaos swallowed me; the Prince of Qin gave me life, and I owe him my body.

sentences.zh: 今於殿下無功，其敢當賜？

translations.literal: Now toward Your Highness he has no merit—how dare he accept gifts?
translations.idiomatic: I have done nothing for Your Highness—how dare I take your gifts?

sentences.zh: 若私許，則懷二心，徇利棄忠，殿下亦焉用之哉？」

translations.literal: If he secretly agreed, he would harbor two hearts, chase profit and abandon loyalty—would Your Highness employ such a one?"
translations.idiomatic: If I secretly agreed, I would be a man of two hearts trading loyalty for gold—what use would Your Highness have for me?"

sentences.zh: 太子怒而止。

translations.literal: The Crown Prince, enraged, desisted.
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince fumed and let it drop.

sentences.zh: 敬德以聞。

translations.literal: Jingde reported it.
translations.idiomatic: Jingde reported the offer to the Prince of Qin.

sentences.zh: 王曰：「公之心如山嶽然，雖積金至斗，豈能移之？

translations.literal: The Prince said: "Your heart is like mountains and peaks—even if gold piled to the peck, how could it be moved?
translations.idiomatic: The Prince said, "Your heart stands like a mountain—even gold heaped to the peck could not shift it.

sentences.zh: 然恐非自安計。」

translations.literal: Yet I fear this is not a plan for your own safety."
translations.idiomatic: But I fear that will not keep you safe."

sentences.zh: 巢王果遣壯士刺之。

translations.literal: Prince Chao indeed sent bravos to assassinate him.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Li Yuanji duly sent assassins.

sentences.zh: 敬德開門安臥，賊至，不敢入。

translations.literal: Jingde opened his door and lay at ease; when the assassins came they did not dare enter.
translations.idiomatic: Jingde left his door open and slept; the killers dared not step inside.

sentences.zh: 因譖於高祖，將殺之，王固爭，得免。

translations.literal: They slandered him to Gaozu, who was about to execute him; the Prince argued fiercely and he was spared.
translations.idiomatic: They denounced him to Gaozu, who nearly had him killed until the Prince argued him free.

sentences.zh: 其後隱、巢計日急，敬德與長孫無忌入白曰：「大王不先決，社稷危矣！」

translations.literal: Afterward the Hidden and Chao princes' plots grew daily urgent; Jingde and Zhangsun Wuji entered to report: "If the Great Prince does not decide first, the altars of state are in peril!"
translations.idiomatic: As Jiancheng and Yuanji tightened their plots, Jingde and Zhangsun Wuji warned, "Unless you act first, the realm is lost!"

sentences.zh: 王曰：「我惟同氣，所未忍。

translations.literal: The Prince said: "We share one breath of kin—I cannot bear it.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince said, "They are my brothers; I cannot bear it.

sentences.zh: 伺其發，而後以義討之，如何？」

translations.literal: Wait until they move, then punish them by righteousness—how would that be?"
translations.idiomatic: Wait until they strike, then answer with justice—would that not do?"

sentences.zh: 敬德曰：「人情畏死，眾以死奉王，此天授也。

translations.literal: Jingde said: "Human hearts fear death; the host is ready to die for the Great Prince—this is Heaven's grant.
translations.idiomatic: Jingde said, "Men fear death, yet yours will die for you—that is Heaven's gift.

sentences.zh: 天與不取，反得其咎。

translations.literal: What Heaven gives and you do not take, you instead receive its blame.
translations.idiomatic: Refuse Heaven's offer and Heaven will blame you.

sentences.zh: 大王即不聽，請從此亡，不能交手蒙戮。」

translations.literal: If the Great Prince will not heed, let this one flee from here—he cannot join hands and accept slaughter."
translations.idiomatic: If you will not listen, I beg leave to flee rather than die disarmed."

sentences.zh: 無忌曰：「王不從敬德言，敬德亦非王有，今敗矣。」

translations.literal: Wuji said: "If the Prince does not follow Jingde's words, Jingde too will not belong to the Prince—defeat is now."
translations.idiomatic: Wuji added, "Without Jingde you are already beaten."

sentences.zh: 王曰：「寡人之謀，未可全棄，公更圖之。」

translations.literal: The Prince said: "Our counsel cannot be wholly cast away—you must plot again."
translations.idiomatic: The Prince said, "Do not abandon every plan—think again."

sentences.zh: 敬德曰：「處事有疑非智，臨難不決非勇。

translations.literal: Jingde said: "To doubt in affairs is not wisdom; to fail to decide facing peril is not courage.
translations.idiomatic: Jingde said, "Doubt in action is not wisdom; hesitation in crisis is not courage.

sentences.zh: 王今自計如何？

translations.literal: How does the Prince reckon for himself now?
translations.idiomatic: What is your own reckoning now?

sentences.zh: 勇士八百人悉入宮控弦被甲矣，尚何辭？」

translations.literal: Eight hundred stalwarts have all entered the palace, strung bows and donned armor—what more is there to say?"
translations.idiomatic: Eight hundred picked men already wait in the palace, armed and strung—what more is there to debate?"

sentences.zh: 後又與侯君集等懇熟勸進，計乃定。

translations.literal: Later, with Hou Junji and others he earnestly and repeatedly urged advance; the plan was then fixed.
translations.idiomatic: Hou Junji and others pressed him again until the decision held.

sentences.zh: 時房玄齡、杜如晦被斥在外，召不至。

translations.literal: At the time Fang Xuanling and Du Ruhui had been dismissed and were outside; summoned, they did not come.
translations.idiomatic: Fang Xuanling and Du Ruhui had been banished and would not answer the summons.

sentences.zh: 王怒曰：「是背我邪？」

translations.literal: The Prince said in anger: "Have they turned against me?"
translations.idiomatic: The Prince raged, "Have they betrayed me?"

sentences.zh: 因解所佩刀反授之。

translations.literal: He therefore unfastened the sword at his belt and handed it back to him.
translations.idiomatic: He drew his sword and handed it over.

sentences.zh: 謂曰：「即不從，可斬其首以來。」

translations.literal: He told him: "If they still will not obey, you may cut off their heads and bring them."
translations.idiomatic: He said, "If they refuse, bring me their heads."

sentences.zh: 敬德遂往諭玄齡等，與入計議。

translations.literal: Jingde then went to instruct Xuanling and the others, and entered with them to deliberate.
translations.idiomatic: Jingde went, persuaded Fang and Du, and brought them in to plan.

sentences.zh: 隱太子死，敬德領騎七十趨玄武門，王馬逸，墜林下，元吉將奪弓窘王，敬德馳叱之，元吉走，遂射殺之。

translations.literal: The Hidden Crown Prince died; Jingde led seventy horsemen rushing to Xuanwu Gate. The Prince's horse bolted and he fell beneath the trees; Yuanji was about to seize the bow and corner the Prince. Jingde galloped shouting at him; Yuanji fled and was then shot dead.
translations.idiomatic: When the crown prince fell, Jingde raced to Xuanwu Gate with seventy riders. The Prince's horse threw him; Yuanji seized his bow—until Jingde charged, Yuanji fled, and Jingde shot him down.

sentences.zh: 宮、府兵屯玄武門，戰不解，敬德持二首示之，乃去。

translations.literal: Palace and princely troops massed at Xuanwu Gate; battle would not end. Jingde held up the two heads to show them, and they dispersed.
translations.idiomatic: Palace and princely troops still fought at the gate until Jingde raised both brothers' heads; then they broke.

sentences.zh: 時帝泛舟海池，王命敬德往侍，不解甲趨行在。

translations.literal: The Emperor was then boating on the Sea Pool; the Prince ordered Jingde to attend him, rushing to the traveling quarters without removing armor.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu was boating on the imperial pool; the Prince sent Jingde, still in armor, to stand guard.

sentences.zh: 帝驚曰：「今日之亂爲誰？

translations.literal: The Emperor said in alarm: "For whom is today's turmoil?
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor started: "Who raised today's tumult?

sentences.zh: 爾來何邪？」

translations.literal: Why have you come?"
translations.idiomatic: Why are you here?"

sentences.zh: 對曰：「秦王以太子、齊王作亂，舉兵誅之，恐陛下不安，遣臣宿衛。」

translations.literal: He answered: "The Prince of Qin, because the Crown Prince and Prince of Qi made rebellion, raised troops to execute them; fearing Your Majesty's unease, he sent this subject to stand night guard."
translations.idiomatic: He answered, "The Prince of Qin put down rebellion by the crown and Qi princes and sent me lest Your Majesty be troubled."

sentences.zh: 帝意悅。

translations.literal: The Emperor's mind was pleased.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor was soothed.

sentences.zh: 於是南衙、北門兵與府兵尚雜鬥，敬德請帝手詔諸軍聽秦王節度，內外始定。

translations.literal: Then southern yamen, northern gate troops, and princely soldiers were still mixed in battle; Jingde asked the Emperor to write by hand ordering all armies to obey the Prince of Qin's command, and inside and outside were then settled.
translations.idiomatic: Fighting still raged between palace guards and princely troops until Jingde had Gaozu write that all armies obey the Prince of Qin; then order returned.

sentences.zh: 王爲皇太子，授左衛率。

translations.literal: The Prince became Crown Prince and was appointed Left Guard commander.
translations.idiomatic: Made crown prince, he named Jingde commander of the left guard.

sentences.zh: 時坐隱、巢者百餘家，將盡沒入之。

translations.literal: At the time more than a hundred households were implicated with the Hidden and Chao princes and were to be wholly confiscated.
translations.idiomatic: More than a hundred families tied to Jiancheng and Yuanji faced confiscation.

sentences.zh: 敬德曰：「爲惡者二人，今已誅，若又窮支黨，非取安之道。」

translations.literal: Jingde said: "Those who did evil were two men; they are now executed—if we again hunt their branches and parties, that is not the way to win peace."
translations.idiomatic: Jingde urged, "Only two men did evil and they are dead—hounding their clans is no path to peace."

sentences.zh: 由是普原。

translations.literal: Thereby all were broadly pardoned.
translations.idiomatic: A general amnesty followed.

sentences.zh: 論功爲第一，賜絹萬匹，舉齊府金幣、什器賜焉。

translations.literal: In merit reckoning he ranked first; ten thousand bolts of silk were bestowed, and the gold, coin, and utensils of the Qi princely house were all given him.
translations.idiomatic: His merit ranked first: ten thousand bolts of silk and the Qi prince's treasury of gold and furnishings.

sentences.zh: 除右武候大將軍，封吳國公，實封千三百戸。

translations.literal: He was made Grand General of the Right Martial Guard, enfeoffed as Duke of Wu, with a substantive fief of thirteen hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: He became grand general of the right martial guard, Duke of Wu, with a fief of thirteen hundred households.

sentences.zh: 突厥入寇，授涇州道行軍總管。

translations.literal: When the Turks invaded, he was appointed campaigning commander of the Jingzhou circuit.
translations.idiomatic: When the Turks raided, he was made campaigning commander on the Jingzhou front.

sentences.zh: 虜至涇陽，輕騎與戰，敗之。

translations.literal: The barbarians reached Jingyang; with light cavalry he fought and defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: He met them at Jingyang with light horse and drove them off.

sentences.zh: 敬德所得財，必散之士卒。

translations.literal: Whatever wealth Jingde obtained he always distributed among the soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: Every prize he won went straight to the ranks.

sentences.zh: 然婞直，頗以功自負，又廷質大臣得失，與宰相不平。

translations.literal: Yet he was obstinate and upright, rather proud of his merit, and at court challenged ministers' right and wrong—he was not on good terms with the chief ministers.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he was blunt, proud of his record, and prone to challenge ministers in open court until he fell out with the chancellors.

sentences.zh: 出爲襄州都督。

translations.literal: He was sent out as military governor of Xiangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was posted as governor of Xiangzhou.

sentences.zh: 累遷同州刺史。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly transferred to prefect of Tongzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He later became prefect of Tongzhou.

sentences.zh: 嘗侍宴慶善宮，有班其上者，敬德曰：「爾何功，坐我上？」

translations.literal: Once attending a feast at Qingshan Palace, someone was ranked above him. Jingde said: "What merit have you, to sit above me?"
translations.idiomatic: At a feast in Qingshan Palace a guest sat above him; Jingde demanded, "What deed of yours outranks mine?"

sentences.zh: 任城王道宗解喻之，敬德勃然，擊道宗目幾眇。

translations.literal: Prince Daozong of Ren City tried to explain; Jingde flared up and struck Daozong, nearly blinding his eye.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Daozong tried to calm him; Jingde struck him and nearly blinded his eye.

sentences.zh: 太宗不懌，罷，召讓曰：「朕觀漢史，嘗怪高祖時功臣少全者。

translations.literal: Taizong was displeased, ended the feast, summoned and reproved him: "When We read Han history, We once wondered why few of Gaozu's merit men ended whole.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong ended the banquet and rebuked him: "Reading Han histories I used to wonder why so few of Gaozu's champions died in bed.

sentences.zh: 今視卿所爲，乃知韓、彭夷戮，非高祖過。

translations.literal: Now seeing what you have done, We know the slaughter of Han Xin and Peng Yue was not Gaozu's fault.
translations.idiomatic: Now I see your conduct and know Gaozu was right to destroy Han Xin and Peng Yue.

sentences.zh: 國之大事，惟賞與罰，橫恩不可數得，勉自脩飭，悔可及乎！」

translations.literal: The great affairs of state are only reward and punishment; reckless favor cannot be gained again and again—strive to discipline yourself; can regret still be reached?"
translations.idiomatic: The state rests on reward and punishment; indulgence cannot be endless—discipline yourself while you still can."

sentences.zh: 敬德頓首謝。

translations.literal: Jingde knocked his head in thanks.
translations.idiomatic: Jingde kowtowed in apology.

sentences.zh: 後改封鄂國，歷鄜、夏二州都督。

translations.literal: Later his fief was changed to the State of E and he served in turn as military governor of Fu and Xia prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: He was later made Duke of E and governed Fu and Xia prefectures.

sentences.zh: 老就第，授開府儀同三司，朝朔望。

translations.literal: In old age he retired to his mansion, was given the title of Honored Companion with Protocol Equal to the Three Excellencies, and attended court on the first and fifteenth.
translations.idiomatic: In old age he retired home as honorary three-excellency equal and came to court on the first and fifteenth of each month.

sentences.zh: 帝將討高麗，敬德上言：「乘輿至遼，太子次定州，兩京空虛，恐有玄感之變。

translations.literal: When the Emperor was about to campaign against Goguryeo, Jingde submitted: "If the imperial carriage reaches Liao, the Crown Prince stations at Dingzhou, and the two capitals stand empty, We fear a change like Xuangan's.
translations.idiomatic: Before the Goguryeo campaign Jingde warned, "If Your Majesty goes to Liao while the crown prince holds Dingzhou and both capitals lie empty, we risk another Yang Xuangan.

sentences.zh: 夷貊小國，不足枉萬乘，願委之將臣，以時摧滅。」

translations.literal: A petty Yi-Mo state is not worth bending the imperial chariot—We wish to entrust it to generals and ministers to crush in due time."
translations.idiomatic: A barbarian fringe state is not worth the Son of Heaven's march—leave it to your generals to crush in season."

sentences.zh: 帝不納。

translations.literal: The Emperor did not accept it.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor would not hear it.

sentences.zh: 詔以本官行太常卿，爲左一馬軍總管。

translations.literal: An edict made him acting Minister of Rites in his present office and commander of the Left First Horse Army.
translations.idiomatic: He was ordered to serve as acting minister of rites and commander of the left first horse army.

sentences.zh: 師還，復致仕。

translations.literal: When the army returned he again retired from office.
translations.idiomatic: When the army returned he retired again.

sentences.zh: 顯慶三年卒，年七十四。

translations.literal: In the third year of Xianqing he died, aged seventy-four.
translations.idiomatic: He died in Xianqing 3 at seventy-four.

sentences.zh: 高宗詔京官五品以上及朝集使赴第臨吊，冊贈司徒、并州都督，謚曰忠武。

translations.literal: Emperor Gaozong ordered capital officials of fifth rank and above and court assembly envoys to his residence for mourning; by patent he was posthumously made Minister of Education and military governor of Bingzhou, posthumous title Loyal Martial.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozong ordered officials of fifth rank and above to mourn at his house, posthumously made him minister of education and Bingzhou governor, with the title Loyal Martial.

sentences.zh: 給班劍、羽葆、鼓吹，陪葬昭陵。

translations.literal: Court swords, feather banners, and martial music were granted; he was buried beside Zhaoling.
translations.idiomatic: He was granted imperial funeral arms and music and buried at Zhaoling.

sentences.zh: 敬德晚節，謝賓客不與通。

translations.literal: In his late years Jingde declined guests and would not associate with them.
translations.idiomatic: In his last years he shut his door to visitors.

sentences.zh: 飭觀、沼，奏清商樂，自奉養甚厚。

translations.literal: He adorned halls and ponds, played Qing Shang music, and nourished himself very richly.
translations.idiomatic: He tended pavilions and ponds, played court music, and lived in lavish ease.

sentences.zh: 又餌雲母粉，爲方士術延年。

translations.literal: He also took mica powder, following alchemical arts to prolong life.
translations.idiomatic: He swallowed mica powder in the hope of longevity.

sentences.zh: 其戰，善避槊，每單騎入賊，雖群刺之不能傷，又能奪取賊槊還刺之。

translations.literal: In battle he excelled at evading the pike; each time he charged alone into the enemy, though many thrust at him they could not wound him, and he could also seize enemy pikes and thrust back.
translations.idiomatic: In battle he could dodge pikes at will, ride alone into enemy ranks untouched by a crowd of thrusts, and snatch a foe's pike to strike back.

sentences.zh: 齊王元吉使去刃與之校，敬德請王加刃，而獨去之，卒不能中。

translations.literal: Prince Qi Yuanji had the blades removed to contest with him; Jingde asked the prince to add blades while he alone removed his, and in the end they could not strike him.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Qi ordered blunt pikes for a trial; Jingde asked that the prince keep edged blades while he fought bare—none could touch him.

sentences.zh: 帝嘗問：「奪槊與避槊孰難？」

translations.literal: The Emperor once asked: "Which is harder—seizing the pike or evading the pike?"
translations.idiomatic: Taizong once asked, "Which is harder—taking a pike or dodging one?"

sentences.zh: 對曰：「奪槊難。」

translations.literal: He answered: "Seizing the pike is harder."
translations.idiomatic: Seizing it," he said."

sentences.zh: 試使與齊王戲，少選，王三失槊，遂大愧服。

translations.literal: They tried him in sport with the Prince of Qi; in a little while the prince lost his pike three times and was greatly shamed into submission.
translations.idiomatic: In a bout with Prince Qi the prince lost his pike three times and admitted defeat.

sentences.zh: 張公謹，字弘慎，魏州繁水人。

translations.literal: Zhang Gongjin—Zhang Gongjin, style Hongshen, a man of Fanshui in Weizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Gongjin (style Hongshen) came from Fanshui in Weizhou.

sentences.zh: 爲王世充洧州長史，與刺史崔樞挈城歸天子，授檢校鄒州別駕，遷累右武候長史，未知名。

translations.literal: He was chief clerk of Weizhou for Wang Shichong; with prefect Cui Shu he brought the city over to the Son of Heaven, was appointed acting vice-prefect of Zouzhou, and through successive transfers became chief clerk of the Right Martial Guard—still not widely known.
translations.idiomatic: As Wang Shichong's chief clerk at Weizhou he and Prefect Cui Shu surrendered the city to the Tang, became acting vice-prefect of Zou, then chief clerk of the right martial guard, still little known.

sentences.zh: 李勣、尉遲敬德數啟秦王，乃引入府。

translations.literal: Li Jing and Yuchi Jingde repeatedly reported to the Prince of Qin, and he was then brought into the princely mansion.
translations.idiomatic: Li Jing and Yuchi Jingde repeatedly recommended him until the Prince of Qin took him into his staff.

sentences.zh: 王將討隱、巢亂，使卜人占之，公謹自外至，投龜於地曰：「凡卜以定猶豫，決嫌疑。

translations.literal: When the Prince was about to settle the Hidden and Chao turmoil he had a diviner cast; Gongjin arrived from outside, threw the tortoise to the ground, and said: "Divination is to settle hesitation and decide doubt.
translations.idiomatic: As the Prince prepared against Jiancheng and Yuanji he called a diviner; Gongjin entered, cast the oracle aside, and said, "One divines to end doubt.

sentences.zh: 今事無疑，何卜之爲？

translations.literal: Now the affair has no doubt—why divine?
translations.idiomatic: There is no doubt here—why cast at all?

sentences.zh: 卜而不吉，其可已乎？」

translations.literal: If you divine and it is not auspicious, can you then stop?"
translations.idiomatic: If the signs were ill, would you then abandon the deed?"

sentences.zh: 王曰：「善。」

translations.literal: The Prince said: "Well said."
translations.idiomatic: The Prince said, "Well spoken."

sentences.zh: 隱太子死，其徒攻玄武門，銳甚，公謹獨閉關拒之。

translations.literal: When the Hidden Crown Prince died his followers attacked Xuanwu Gate with fierce force; Gongjin alone barred the gate and held them off.
translations.idiomatic: When the crown prince fell his men stormed Xuanwu Gate; Gongjin alone barred the gate and held them.

sentences.zh: 以功授左武候將軍，封定遠郡公，實封一千戸。

translations.literal: For merit he was made General of the Left Martial Guard, enfeoffed as Duke of Dingyuan commandery, with a substantive fief of one thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: For this he became general of the left martial guard, Duke of Dingyuan, with a fief of one thousand households.

sentences.zh: 貞觀初，爲代州都督，置屯田以省饋運。

translations.literal: Early in Zhenguan he was military governor of Daizhou and established garrison farms to economize on transport of supplies.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Zhenguan he governed Daizhou and opened garrison farms to cut supply costs.

sentences.zh: 數言時政得失，太宗多所采納。

translations.literal: He often spoke on the gains and losses of current policy; Taizong adopted much of it.
translations.idiomatic: He spoke frankly on policy and Taizong often took his advice.

sentences.zh: 後副李靖經略突厥，條可取狀於帝曰：「頡利縱欲肆凶，誅害善良，昵近小人，此主昏於上，可取一也。

translations.literal: Later, assisting Li Jing in planning against the Turks, he itemized grounds for taking them and said to the Emperor: "Jieli indulges desire and unleashes cruelty, executes the good, and dotes on petty men—this is a ruler benighted above; he may be taken, first point.
translations.idiomatic: Later, under Li Jing against the Turks, he listed six reasons to strike: "Jieli indulges cruelty, kills the worthy, and trusts flatterers—the ruler above is blind; that is the first reason.

sentences.zh: 別部同羅、仆骨、回紇、延陀之屬，皆自立君長，圖爲反噬，此眾叛於下，可取二也。

translations.literal: Separate tribes Tongluo, Pugu, Uyghur, Yenisei, and the like have all set up their own chiefs and plot to turn and bite—this is the masses rebelling below; he may be taken, second point.
translations.idiomatic: The Tongluo, Pugu, Uyghurs, Yenisei Kirghiz, and others each crown their own chiefs and plot revolt—the tribes below are divided; second reason.

sentences.zh: 突利被疑，以輕騎免，拓設出討，眾敗無余，欲谷喪師，無托足之地，此兵挫將敗，可取三也。

translations.literal: Tuli is suspected and escaped with light horse; Tuoshe went out to campaign and his host was broken without remainder; Yugu lost his army and has no footing—this is troops defeated and generals ruined; he may be taken, third point.
translations.idiomatic: Tuli fled under suspicion; Tuoshe's expedition was wiped out; Yugu's army is broken with nowhere to stand—the armies are shattered; third reason.

sentences.zh: 北方霜旱，稟糧乏絕，可取四也。

translations.literal: The north has frost and drought; stored grain is exhausted—he may be taken, fourth point.
translations.idiomatic: Frost and drought have emptied their granaries in the north; fourth reason.

sentences.zh: 頡利疏突厥，親諸胡，胡性翻覆，大軍臨之，內必生變，可取五也。

translations.literal: Jieli is estranged from the Turks and close to the various Hu; Hu nature is fickle—when the great army presses, within there will surely be change; he may be taken, fifth point.
translations.idiomatic: Jieli alienates the Turks and favors the frontier peoples, whose loyalties shift—when our army comes, they will turn on him; fifth reason.

sentences.zh: 華人在北者甚眾，比聞屯聚，保據山險，王師之出，當有應者，可取六也。」

translations.literal: Chinese in the north are very numerous; recently it is heard they gather in strongholds on perilous mountains—when the royal army goes forth there should be responders; he may be taken, sixth point."
translations.idiomatic: Many Chinese in the north have lately gathered in mountain strongholds—they will rise when our columns march; sixth reason."

sentences.zh: 帝然所謀。

translations.literal: The Emperor approved the plan.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 及破定襄，敗頡利，璽詔慰勞，進封鄒國公，改襄州都督，以惠政聞。

translations.literal: When Dingxiang was broken and Jieli defeated, an imperial letter comforted and rewarded him; he was advanced to Duke of Zou, transferred to military governor of Xiangzhou, and was famed for benevolent government.
translations.idiomatic: After Dingxiang fell and Jieli was beaten, an imperial letter praised him; he was made Duke of Zou, governor of Xiangzhou, and famed for humane rule.

sentences.zh: 卒官下，年四十九。

translations.literal: He died in office, aged forty-nine.
translations.idiomatic: He died in office at forty-nine.

sentences.zh: 帝將出次哭之，有司奏：「日在辰，不可。」

translations.literal: The Emperor was about to go out in person to mourn him; the relevant offices reported: "The day is in the chen hour—it is not permissible."
translations.idiomatic: Taizong meant to mourn him in person; the calendar office objected that the hour was inauspicious."

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「君臣猶父子也，情感於內，安有所避。」

translations.literal: The Emperor said: "Minister and ruler are like father and son; feeling moves within—how could there be avoidance?"
translations.idiomatic: Taizong said, "A minister and his lord are as father and son—when grief moves the heart, what omen can I heed?"

sentences.zh: 遂哭之。

translations.literal: Thereupon he wept for him.
translations.idiomatic: He went ahead and wept for him.

sentences.zh: 詔贈左驍衛大將軍，謚曰襄。

translations.literal: An edict posthumously conferred Left Brave Guard General-in-Chief; posthumous title Xiang.
translations.idiomatic: An edict awarded him posthumously the rank of Left Brave Guard General-in-Chief, with the posthumous name Xiang.

sentences.zh: 十三年，追改郯國公。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year, posthumously changed to Duke of Tan.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year of Zhenguan, his title was posthumously raised to Duke of Tan.

sentences.zh: 永徽中，加贈荊州都督。

translations.literal: In the Yonghui era, additionally posthumously conferred Regional Inspector of Jingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: During the Yonghui reign, he received the additional posthumous appointment as Regional Inspector of Jingzhou.

sentences.zh: 公謹子 大素子大素，龍朔中，歷東臺舍人，兼修國史，著書百餘篇，終懷州長史。

translations.literal: Gongjin's son Dasu: Dasu, in the Longshuo era, served as Eastern Terrace Attendant, also editing the national history; he wrote more than a hundred works and ended as Chief Administrator of Huaizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Gongjin's son Dasu served during Longshuo as an Eastern Terrace attendant and as a compiler of the national history; he authored more than a hundred works and died as chief administrator of Huaizhou.

sentences.zh: 次子大安，上元中，同中書門下三品。

translations.literal: The second son Da'an, in the Shangyuan era, was Associate of the Secretariat-Chancellery with Third Rank.
translations.idiomatic: His second son Da'an rose during Shangyuan to the rank of associate grand councilor.

sentences.zh: 章懷太子令與劉訥言等共註范曄《漢書》。

translations.literal: Crown Prince Zhanghuai ordered him, together with Liu Neyan and others, jointly to annotate Fan Ye's Book of Han.
translations.idiomatic: Crown Prince Zhanghuai had him work with Liu Neyan and others on a commentary to Fan Ye's Book of Han.

sentences.zh: 太子廢，故貶爲普州刺史，終橫州司馬。

translations.literal: When the crown prince was deposed, he was therefore demoted to Prefect of Puzhou and ended as Military Adjutant of Hengzhou.
translations.idiomatic: After the crown prince's deposition he was demoted to prefect of Puzhou and ended his career as military adjutant of Hengzhou.

sentences.zh: 子悱，仕玄宗時爲集賢院判官，詔以其家所著《魏書》、《說林》入院，綴修所闕，累擢知圖書、括訪異書使，進國子司業，以累免官。

translations.literal: His son Fei, serving in Emperor Xuanzong's time as Collegium Academiae Assessor, was ordered that his family's writings The Book of Wei and Shuolin enter the academy; he patched missing portions, was repeatedly promoted to Commissioner for Books and Searcher of Rare Books, advanced to Vice-Director of the Directorate of Education, and was dismissed from office because of entanglements.
translations.idiomatic: His son Fei served under Emperor Xuanzong as an assessor of the Hall of Worthies; the court ordered the family's Book of Wei and Forest of Sayings into the imperial library, where Fei filled lacunae. He rose to commissioner of books and searcher of rare texts, then vice-director of the Directorate of Education, but lost his post after becoming implicated in a scandal.

sentences.zh: 秦瓊，字叔寶，以字顯，齊州歷城人。

translations.literal: Qin Qiong, style name Shubao, known by his style name, a man of Licheng in Qizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Qin Qiong, known by his style Shubao, was a native of Licheng in Qizhou.

sentences.zh: 始爲隋將來護兒帳內，母喪，護兒遣使襚弔之。

translations.literal: At first he was in the tent retinue of the Sui general Lai Hu'er; when his mother died, Hu'er sent an envoy with funeral gifts to offer condolences.
translations.idiomatic: He began his career in the personal guard of the Sui general Lai Hu'er. When his mother died, Hu'er sent an envoy with funeral gifts to mourn with him.

sentences.zh: 吏怪曰：「士卒死喪，將軍未有所問，今獨弔叔寶何也？」

translations.literal: An official said in surprise: "When soldiers die in mourning, the general has never inquired—why now mourn Shubao alone?"
translations.idiomatic: A staff officer asked in surprise, "When ordinary soldiers lose kin, you never take notice—why send condolences only to Shubao?"

sentences.zh: 護兒曰：「是子才而武，志節完整，豈久處卑賤邪？」

translations.literal: Hu'er said: "This lad is talented and martial, his will and integrity whole—how could he long remain in low station?"
translations.idiomatic: Hu'er replied, "This man has talent and courage, and his integrity is intact—how could he stay in a humble post for long?"

sentences.zh: 俄從通守張須陀擊賊盧明月下邳，賊眾十餘萬，須陀所統才十之一，堅壁水敢進，糧盡，欲引去。

translations.literal: Soon he followed Circuit Defender Zhang Xutuo to strike the bandit Lu Mingyue at Xiapi; the rebels numbered more than a hundred thousand, while Xutuo commanded only a tenth of that force. They held their walls and dared not advance over the water; when provisions were exhausted, they wished to withdraw.
translations.idiomatic: He soon followed Zhang Xutuo, defender of Tong circuit, against the rebel Lu Mingyue at Xiapi. The rebels numbered over a hundred thousand; Xutuo had barely a tenth as many. The government troops held their camp and would not cross the water; when grain ran out, they prepared to retreat.

sentences.zh: 須陀曰：「賊見兵卻，必悉眾追我，得銳士襲其營，且有利，誰爲吾行者？」

translations.literal: Xutuo said: "When the bandits see our troops withdraw, they will surely muster all their forces to pursue us. If elite men can strike their camp, there will be advantage—who will go for me?"
translations.idiomatic: Xutuo said, "Once the rebels see us pull back, they will throw their whole army in pursuit. If bold men can raid their camp, we still have a chance—who will go for me?"

sentences.zh: 眾莫對。

translations.literal: None answered.
translations.idiomatic: No one answered.

sentences.zh: 惟叔寶與羅士信奮行。

translations.literal: Only Shubao and Luo Shixin stepped forward with ardor to go.
translations.idiomatic: Only Shubao and Luo Shixin volunteered and set out.

sentences.zh: 乃分勁兵千人伏莽間，須陀委營遁，明月悉兵追躡。

translations.literal: They then divided a thousand crack troops to lie in ambush in the thickets; Xutuo abandoned the camp and fled, and Mingyue mustered all his troops in pursuit.
translations.idiomatic: They hid a thousand picked troops in the brush. Xutuo abandoned camp and withdrew; Mingyue threw his whole force in pursuit.

sentences.zh: 叔寶等馳叩賊營，門閉不得入，乃升樓拔賊旗幟，殺數十人，營中亂，即斬關納外兵，縱火焚三十餘屯。

translations.literal: Shubao and the others galloped to strike the rebel camp; the gates were shut and they could not enter, so they climbed a tower, pulled down the rebel banners and flags, killed several tens of men, threw the camp into disorder, then cut the pass and admitted the outside troops, and set fires burning more than thirty stockades.
translations.idiomatic: Shubao and his party galloped into the rebel camp. The gates were shut, so they scaled a tower, tore down rebel banners, and killed dozens of men until the camp fell into chaos. They then broke the gate, let in the outside force, and burned more than thirty encampments.

sentences.zh: 明月奔還，須陀回擊，大破之。

translations.literal: Mingyue ran back; Xutuo turned and struck, routing them utterly.
translations.idiomatic: Mingyue raced back in disarray; Xutuo wheeled and attacked, winning a crushing victory.

sentences.zh: 又與孫宣雅戰海曲，先登。

translations.literal: Again he fought Sun Xuanya at Haiqu and was first to scale the walls.
translations.idiomatic: He also fought Sun Xuanya at Haiqu and was the first man over the wall.

sentences.zh: 以前後功擢建節尉。

translations.literal: For cumulative merit before and after, he was promoted to Establishment-Banner Commandant.
translations.idiomatic: For these and other feats he was promoted to Establishment-Banner commandant.

sentences.zh: 從須陀擊李密滎陽。

translations.literal: He followed Xutuo to strike Li Mi at Xingyang.
translations.idiomatic: He followed Xutuo against Li Mi at Xingyang.

sentences.zh: 須陀死，率殘兵附裴仁基。

translations.literal: When Xutuo died, he led the remnant troops to join Pei Renji.
translations.idiomatic: After Xutuo's death he led the survivors to Pei Renji.

sentences.zh: 仁基降密，密得叔寶大喜，以爲帳內驃騎，待之甚厚。

translations.literal: Renji surrendered to Mi; Mi, gaining Shubao, was greatly pleased and made him tent-inner swift-cavalry commander, treating him very generously.
translations.idiomatic: When Renji surrendered to Li Mi, Mi was overjoyed to gain Shubao and made him a swift-cavalry commander in his personal guard, treating him with exceptional favor.

sentences.zh: 密與宇文化及戰黎陽，中矢墮馬，濱死，追兵至，獨叔寶捍衛得免。

translations.literal: Mi fought Yuwen Huaji at Liyang, was struck by an arrow and fell from his horse, on the brink of death; pursuers arrived, and Shubao alone defended him so he escaped.
translations.idiomatic: When Mi fought Yuwen Huaji at Liyang he was shot from his horse and nearly killed. Pursuers closed in; only Shubao's defense saved him.

sentences.zh: 後歸王世充，署龍驤大將軍。

translations.literal: Later he returned to Wang Shichong and was appointed Dragon-Flight Grand General.
translations.idiomatic: He later entered the service of Wang Shichong, who appointed him Dragon-Flight grand general.

sentences.zh: 與程咬金計曰：「世充多詐，數與下咒誓，乃巫嫗，非撥亂主也。」

translations.literal: He plotted with Cheng Yaojin, saying: "Shichong is greatly deceitful, often making oaths and spells with his subordinates—he is a witch-woman, not a lord who can settle chaos."
translations.idiomatic: He and Cheng Yaojin agreed: "Shichong is treacherous, forever binding his men with oaths and sorcery—he is a charlatan, not a ruler who can restore order."

sentences.zh: 因約俱西走，策其馬謝世充曰：「自顧不能奉事，請從此辭。」

translations.literal: They therefore agreed to flee west together; spurring their horses, they took leave of Shichong, saying: "Seeing that we cannot serve you, we beg leave from here."
translations.idiomatic: They agreed to flee west together. Spurring their horses, they told Shichong, "We find we can no longer serve you and take our leave."

sentences.zh: 賊不敢逼，於是來降。

translations.literal: The enemy did not dare press them, and so they came to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: No pursuer dared close on them, and they reached Tang territory to surrender.

sentences.zh: 高祖俾事秦王府，王尤獎禮。

translations.literal: Gaozu had him serve the Prince of Qin's household; the prince especially rewarded and honored him.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu assigned him to the Prince of Qin's household, where the prince treated him with special esteem.

sentences.zh: 從鎮長春宮，拜馬軍總管。

translations.literal: He followed in garrisoning Changchun Palace and was appointed Commander of the Horse Army.
translations.idiomatic: He helped garrison Changchun Palace and was made commander of the horse army.

sentences.zh: 戰美良川，破尉遲敬德，功多，帝賜以黃金瓶，勞曰：「卿不恤妻子而來歸我，且又立功，使朕肉可食，當割以啖爾，況子女玉帛乎！」

translations.literal: He fought at Meiliang River and defeated Yuchi Jingde; his merit was great. The emperor bestowed a golden flask and said in consolation: "You did not care for wife and children in coming to join me, and moreover established merit—if my flesh could be eaten, I ought to cut it to feed you, how much more sons and daughters, jade, and silks!"
translations.idiomatic: At Meiliang River he defeated Yuchi Jingde and won great credit. The emperor gave him a golden flask and said, "You left your family to join me and have already earned merit. If my own flesh could nourish you, I would cut it for you—how much more readily sons, daughters, jade, and silk!"

sentences.zh: 尋授秦王右三統軍，走宋金剛於介休，拜上柱國。

translations.literal: Soon he was appointed the Prince of Qin's Right Third Army Commander; he drove Song Jingang from Jiexiu and was enfeoffed as Pillar of State.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon made the prince's third commander of the right wing, routed Song Jingang at Jiexiu, and was enfeoffed as Pillar of State.

sentences.zh: 從討世充、建德、黑闥三盜，未嘗不身先鋒鏖陣，前無堅對。

translations.literal: In campaigns against the three rebels Shichong, Jiande, and Heita, never did he fail to take the vanguard personally in fierce battle; before him no solid opposition stood.
translations.idiomatic: In the campaigns against Shichong, Jiande, and Heita he always led the van in the hottest fighting; no enemy line held before him.

sentences.zh: 積賜金帛以千萬計，進封翼國公。

translations.literal: Rewards of gold and silks accumulated to tens of millions; he was advanced to Duke of Yi.
translations.idiomatic: Rewards in gold and silk mounted into the millions, and he was advanced to Duke of Yi.

sentences.zh: 每敵有驍將銳士震耀出入以誇眾者，秦王輒命叔寶往取之，躍馬挺槍刺於萬眾中，莫不如志，以是頗自負。

translations.literal: Whenever the enemy had fierce generals and sharp warriors who flashed in and out to awe the masses, the Prince of Qin would order Shubao to go take them; leaping his horse and thrusting his spear amid tens of thousands, none failed to meet his aim—therefore he was rather self-assured.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever enemy champions rode out to dazzle the ranks, the Prince of Qin sent Shubao to bring them down. He would charge into ten thousand men and strike with his spear as he pleased; he rarely missed, and he knew his own worth.

sentences.zh: 及平隱、巢，功拜左武衛大將軍，實封七百戸。

translations.literal: When the Hidden Crown Prince and the Prince of Qin were settled, for merit he was appointed Left Martial Guard General-in-Chief with a substantive fief of seven hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: After the succession struggle was settled, his merit earned him the post of Left Martial Guard general-in-chief and a substantive fief of seven hundred households.

sentences.zh: 後稍移疾，嘗曰：「吾少長戎馬間，歷二百餘戰，數重創，出血且數斛，安得不病乎？」

translations.literal: Later he gradually fell ill and once said: "I grew up from youth amid war-horses, passed through more than two hundred battles, suffered repeated grave wounds, and lost blood amounting to several hu—how could I not be ill?"
translations.idiomatic: He later fell ill and once said, "I have lived my life in the saddle—more than two hundred battles, wound after wound, blood enough to fill several hu. How could my body not fail?"

sentences.zh: 卒，贈徐州都督，陪葬昭陵。

translations.literal: He died; posthumously conferred Regional Inspector of Xuzhou and buried with honor at Zhaoling.
translations.idiomatic: He died. The court posthumously made him regional inspector of Xuzhou and buried him beside Zhaoling.

sentences.zh: 太宗詔有司琢石爲人馬立墓前，以旌戰功。

translations.literal: Taizong ordered the relevant offices to carve stone into human and horse forms to stand before the tomb, to display battle merit.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong ordered officials to carve stone figures of man and horse for his tomb, commemorating his battlefield deeds.

sentences.zh: 貞觀十三年，改封胡國公。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year of Zhenguan, his title was changed to Duke of Hu.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year of Zhenguan his title was changed to Duke of Hu.

sentences.zh: 後四年，詔司徒、趙國公無忌，司空、河間王孝恭，司空、萊國公如晦，司空、太子太師、鄭國公徵，司空、梁國公玄齡，開府儀同三司、鄂國公敬德，特進、衛國公靖，特進、宋國公瑀，輔國大將軍、褒國公志玄，輔國大將軍、夔國公弘基，尚書左僕射、蔣國公通，陜東道行臺右僕射、鄖國公開山，荊州都督、譙國公紹，荊州都督、邳國公順德，洛州都督、鄖國公亮，吏部尚書、陳國公君集，左驍衛大將玖惲郯國公公謹，左領軍大將軍、盧國公知節，禮部尚書、永興郡公世南，戸部尚書、渝國公政會，戸部尚書、莒國公檢，兵部尚書、英國公勣，并叔寶，並圖形凌煙閣。

translations.literal: Four years later, an edict ordered that the merit ministers—including Wuji, Xiaogong, Ruhui, Wei, Xuanling, Jingde, Li Jing, Yu, Zhixuan, Hongji, Qu Tuntong, Kaishan, Shao, Shunde, Liang, Hou Junji, Zhang Gongjin, Cheng Zhijie, Yu Shinan, Zhenghui, Tang Jian, Li Ji, together with Shubao—should all have their portraits painted in the Lingyan Pavilion.
translations.idiomatic: Four years later an edict ordered portraits in the Lingyan Pavilion for the founding meritocrats, including Wuji, Xiaogong, Ruhui, Wei, Xuanling, Jingde, Li Jing, Yu, Zhixuan, Hongji, Qu Tuntong, Kaishan, Shao, Shunde, Liang, Hou Junji, Zhang Gongjin, Cheng Zhijie, Yu Shinan, Zhenghui, Tang Jian, Li Ji, and Shubao.

sentences.zh: 高宗永徽六年，遣使致祭名臣圖形凌煙閣者凡七人，徵、士廉、瑀、志玄、弘基、世南、叔寶，皆始終著名者也。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Yonghui under Gaozong, envoys were sent to offer sacrifice to the famous ministers whose portraits were in the Lingyan Pavilion—seven men in all: Wei, Shiliang, Yu, Zhixuan, Hongji, Shinan, and Shubao—all famed from beginning to end.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year of Yonghui, Emperor Gaozong sent envoys to sacrifice before seven Lingyan portraits—Wei, Shiliang, Yu, Zhixuan, Hongji, Shinan, and Shubao—men whose fame had endured from first to last.

sentences.zh: 唐儉，字茂約，并州晉陽人。

translations.literal: Tang Jian, style name Maoyue, a man of Jinyang in Bingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Tang Jian, style Maoyue, was a native of Jinyang in Bingzhou.

sentences.zh: 祖邕，北齊尚書左僕射。

translations.literal: His grandfather Yong was Northern Qi Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Yong served the Northern Qi as left vice director of the Department of State Affairs.

sentences.zh: 父鑒，隋戎州刺史；

translations.literal: His father Jian was Sui Prefect of Rongzhou;
translations.idiomatic: his father Jian was prefect of Rongzhou under the Sui;

sentences.zh: 與高祖善，嘗偕典軍衛，故儉雅與秦王遊，同在太原。

translations.literal: he was on good terms with Gaozu and once together managed military guard duties, so Jian from youth associated with the Prince of Qin in friendship, both in Taiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: and was close to Gaozu, having once shared command of the guard. Jian therefore grew up alongside the Prince of Qin in Taiyuan.

sentences.zh: 儉爽邁少繩檢，然事親以孝聞。

translations.literal: Jian was open and bold, little bound by restraint, yet in serving his parents he was known for filial piety.
translations.idiomatic: Jian was free-spirited and little given to restraint, yet he was known for filial devotion to his parents.

sentences.zh: 見隋政浸亂，陰說秦王建大計。

translations.literal: Seeing Sui government gradually in disorder, he secretly urged the Prince of Qin to form a great plan.
translations.idiomatic: As Sui rule crumbled, he quietly urged the Prince of Qin to seize the larger design of empire.

sentences.zh: 高祖嘗召訪之，儉曰：「公日角龍庭，姓協圖讖，系天下望久矣。

translations.literal: Gaozu once summoned and questioned him; Jian said: "Your lordship has the sun-horn and dragon-forehead; your surname accords with chart and prophecy—you have borne the hopes of the realm long.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu once asked his counsel. Jian said, "My lord, your brow bears heaven's mark and your name fits the prophecies—the realm has looked to you for years.

sentences.zh: 若外嘯豪傑，北招戎狄，右收燕、趙，濟河而南，以據秦、雍，湯、武之業也。」

translations.literal: If outward you rally heroes, northward summon the Rong and Di, rightward gather Yan and Zhao, cross the river southward, and hold Qin and Yong, it is the enterprise of Tang and Wu."
translations.idiomatic: Rally the heroes abroad, call the northern tribes, secure Yan and Zhao to the east, cross the Yellow River south, and hold Qin and Yong—you would repeat the work of Tang and Wu."

sentences.zh: 高祖曰：「湯、武之事豈可幾？

translations.literal: Gaozu said: "How could the deeds of Tang and Wu be approached?
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu replied, "How could one aspire to Tang and Wu?

sentences.zh: 然喪亂方剡，私當圖存，公欲拯溺者，吾方爲公思之。」

translations.literal: Yet chaos and ruin are just arising; privately one must plan to survive—if your lordship wishes to rescue the drowning, I am just now thinking for your lordship."
translations.idiomatic: Yet the realm is collapsing and each man must first save himself. If you mean to rescue the drowning, I will think through it with you."

sentences.zh: 及大將軍府開，授記室參軍、渭北道元帥司馬。

translations.literal: When the Grand General's Office opened, he was appointed Recorder Staff Officer and Wei-North Circuit Marshal's Major.
translations.idiomatic: When the grand general's office opened, he became recorder staff officer and marshal's major on the Wei-North circuit.

sentences.zh: 從定京師，爲相國府記室，晉昌郡公。

translations.literal: He followed in pacifying the capital, became Recorder of the Chancellor's Office, and was enfeoffed as Duke of Jinchang.
translations.idiomatic: He helped pacify the capital, served as recorder in the chancellor's office, and was enfeoffed as Duke of Jinchang.

sentences.zh: 武德初，進內史舍人，遷中書侍郎、散騎常侍。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Wude he was advanced to Inner Secretariat Attendant, then transferred to Secretariat Vice Director and Regular Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Wude he rose to inner secretariat attendant, then to secretariat vice director and regular attendant.

sentences.zh: 呂崇茂以夏縣反，與劉武周連和，詔永安王孝基、獨孤懷恩，於筠率兵致討，儉以使適至軍。

translations.literal: Lü Chongmao rebelled from Xia County and allied with Liu Wuzhou; an edict ordered Prince of Yong'an Xiaoji, Dugu Huai'en, and Yu Yun to lead troops to punish them. Jian, as envoy, happened to reach the army.
translations.idiomatic: When Lü Chongmao rebelled at Xia County and joined Liu Wuzhou, the court sent Prince Xiaoji, Dugu Huai'en, and Yu Yun against them. Jian arrived on embassy just as the army marched.

sentences.zh: 會孝基等爲武周所虜，儉亦見禽。

translations.literal: It happened that Xiaoji and the others were captured by Wuzhou, and Jian was also taken.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaoji's force was captured by Wuzhou, and Jian with it.

sentences.zh: 始，懷恩屯蒲州，陰與部將元君實謀反，會俱在賊中，君實私語儉曰：「獨孤尚書將舉兵圖大事，猶豫不發，故及此。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Huai'en was garrisoned at Puzhou, he had secretly plotted rebellion with his subordinate Yuan Junshi; now, all being in the enemy's hands, Junshi spoke privately to Jian, saying: "Minister Dugu was about to raise troops for a great affair but hesitated and did not act—hence we have come to this.
translations.idiomatic: Huai'en had once garrisoned Puzhou and secretly plotted rebellion with his officer Yuan Junshi. Now, prisoners together, Junshi whispered to Jian, "Minister Dugu meant to raise troops but wavered—and here we are.

sentences.zh: 所謂當斷不斷而受亂者。」

translations.literal: What is called: when one should decide and does not decide, one suffers disorder.
translations.idiomatic: It is the old fault: failing to strike when one must, and inviting ruin."

sentences.zh: 俄而懷恩脫歸，詔復守蒲。

translations.literal: Soon Huai'en escaped and returned; an edict restored him to guard Pu.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Huai'en escaped home and was ordered back to defend Pu.
