sentences.zh: 君實曰：「獨孤拔難歸，再戍河上，寧其王者不死乎？」

translations.literal: Junshi said: "Dugu, pulling free from hardship, returns and again garrisons the river north—can his kingly ambition be dead?"
translations.idiomatic: Junshi said, "Dugu clawed his way back and again holds the north bank—do you think his royal ambition is dead?"

sentences.zh: 儉恐必亂，密遣劉世讓歸白髮其謀。

translations.literal: Jian feared disorder was certain and secretly sent Liu Shirang back to report and expose the plot.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing revolt, Jian secretly sent Liu Shirang home to expose the plot.

sentences.zh: 會高祖幸蒲津，舟及中流而世讓至，帝驚，曰：「豈非天也！」

translations.literal: It happened that Gaozu was visiting Pujin; when the boat reached midstream Shirang arrived. The emperor was startled and said: "Is this not Heaven's doing!"
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu happened to be at Pujin. Mid-river, Shirang arrived with the warning. The emperor started and cried, "Heaven itself sent this!"

sentences.zh: 命趨還舟，捕反者，懷恩自殺，余黨皆誅。

translations.literal: He ordered a hurried return of the boat, arrested the rebels; Huai'en killed himself, and the remaining partisans were all executed.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered the boat about, seized the rebels, and Huai'en killed himself while his followers were put to death.

sentences.zh: 俄而武周敗，亡入突厥。

translations.literal: Soon Wuzhou was defeated and fled into the Turks.
translations.idiomatic: Wuzhou was soon defeated and fled to the Turks.

sentences.zh: 儉封府庫、籍兵甲以待秦王。

translations.literal: Jian sealed the treasuries and registered armor and weapons to await the Prince of Qin.
translations.idiomatic: Jian sealed the treasuries and inventoried arms for the Prince of Qin.

sentences.zh: 帝嘉儉身幽辱而不忘朝廷，詔復舊官，仍爲并州道安撫大使，許以便宜。

translations.literal: The emperor praised Jian for enduring captivity and disgrace yet not forgetting the court; an edict restored his former office and again made him Pacification Commissioner of Bingzhou Circuit, granting discretionary authority.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor praised Jian for loyalty through captivity, restored his rank, and again made him pacification commissioner of Bingzhou with discretionary powers.

sentences.zh: 盡簿懷恩財產賜儉。

translations.literal: The full register of Huai'en's property was bestowed on Jian.
translations.idiomatic: Huai'en's entire estate was inventoried and given to Jian.

sentences.zh: 還爲禮部尚書、天策府長史、檢校黃門侍郎、莒國公。

translations.literal: On return he became Minister of Rites, Chief Administrator of the Heavenly Policy Office, Acting Yellow Gate Vice Director, and Duke of Ju.
translations.idiomatic: Back at court he became minister of rites, chief administrator of the Heavenly Policy Office, acting yellow gate vice director, and Duke of Ju.

sentences.zh: 仍爲遂州都督，食綿州六百戸。

translations.literal: He was also Regional Inspector of Suizhou, with an income of six hundred households from Mianzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He also served as regional inspector of Suizhou, drawing income from six hundred households in Mianzhou.

sentences.zh: 貞觀初，使突厥還，太宗謂儉曰：「卿觀頡利可取乎？」

translations.literal: At the beginning of Zhenguan, returning from an embassy to the Turks, Taizong said to Jian: "Do you judge Jieli can be taken?"
translations.idiomatic: Early in Zhenguan, on his return from the Turks, Taizong asked Jian, "Do you think Jieli can be taken?"

sentences.zh: 對曰：「銜國威靈，庶有成功。」

translations.literal: He replied: "Bearing the state's august might, there may be success."
translations.idiomatic: He answered, "With the empire's authority behind us, we may succeed."

sentences.zh: 四年，馳傳往誘使歸款，頡利許之，兵懈弛，李靖因襲破之，儉脫身還。

translations.literal: In the fourth year, by rapid relay he went to entice surrender; Jieli agreed, troops grew slack, and Li Jing therefore struck and broke them. Jian escaped and returned.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year he rode posthaste to entice Jieli's surrender. Jieli agreed and his guard relaxed; Li Jing struck and shattered him. Jian escaped and returned.

sentences.zh: 歲餘，爲民部尚書。

translations.literal: After more than a year, he became Minister of the Civil Ministry.
translations.idiomatic: A year later he became minister of the civil ministry.

sentences.zh: 從獵洛陽苑，群豕突出於林，帝射四發，輒殪四豕。

translations.literal: Following a hunt in the Luoyang park, a herd of boars burst from the woods; the emperor shot four times and each time killed a boar.
translations.idiomatic: On a hunt in the Luoyang park a drove of boars charged from the woods. The emperor fired four arrows and dropped four boars.

sentences.zh: 一豕躍及鐙，儉投馬搏之。

translations.literal: One boar leaped to the stirrup; Jian cast himself from the horse to grapple it.
translations.idiomatic: One boar leaped at his stirrup; Jian threw himself from the saddle to fight it off.

sentences.zh: 帝拔劍斷豕，顧笑曰：「天策長史不見上將擊賊邪，何懼之甚？」

translations.literal: The emperor drew his sword and severed the boar, then turned smiling and said: "Chief Administrator of the Heavenly Policy Office—have you not seen a supreme commander strike bandits? Why so much fear?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor drew his sword and cut the boar down, then laughed and said, "Heavenly Policy chief administrator—have you never watched a commander strike down the enemy? Why so frightened?"

sentences.zh: 對曰：「漢祖以馬上得之，不以馬上治之。

translations.literal: He replied: "The Han founder won the realm on horseback but did not rule it on horseback.
translations.idiomatic: Jian answered, "The founder of Han won the realm from horseback but did not govern it from horseback.

sentences.zh: 陛下神武定四方，豈復快心於一獸？」

translations.literal: Your Majesty, by divine martial prowess has settled the four quarters—how could you again take delight in a single beast?"
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty's divine prowess has settled the four quarters—why take pleasure in a single beast?"

sentences.zh: 帝爲罷獵。

translations.literal: The emperor therefore ended the hunt.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ended the hunt.

sentences.zh: 詔其子善識尚豫章公主。

translations.literal: An edict ordered his son Shanshi to marry the Princess of Yuzhang.
translations.idiomatic: An edict married his son Shanshi to the Princess of Yuzhang.

sentences.zh: 悸事，與賓客縱酒爲樂。

translations.literal: He shunned official business and with guests gave himself to wine for pleasure.
translations.idiomatic: He shunned official business and drank with his guests for pleasure.

sentences.zh: 坐小法，貶光祿大夫。

translations.literal: For a minor offense he was demoted to Grand Master for Splendid Happiness.
translations.idiomatic: A minor offense demoted him to grand master for splendid happiness.

sentences.zh: 永徽初，致仕，加特進。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Yonghui he retired from office and was given Special Advancement.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Yonghui he retired and received the rank of special advancement.

sentences.zh: 顯慶初卒，年七十八。

translations.literal: He died at the beginning of Xianqing, aged seventy-eight.
translations.idiomatic: He died early in Xianqing at seventy-eight.

sentences.zh: 贈開府儀同三司、并州都督，陪葬昭陵，謚曰襄。

translations.literal: Posthumously conferred Honored Attendant with Equal Protocol and Regional Inspector of Bingzhou; buried with honor at Zhaoling; posthumous title Xiang.
translations.idiomatic: The court posthumously made him honored attendant with equal protocol and regional inspector of Bingzhou, buried him beside Zhaoling, and gave him the posthumous name Xiang.

sentences.zh: 少子觀，爲河西令，知名。

translations.literal: His youngest son Guan was Magistrate of Hexi and was well known.
translations.idiomatic: His youngest son Guan, magistrate of Hexi, was well known.

sentences.zh: 孫從心，神龍中，以其子脧娶太平公主女，擢累殿中監。

translations.literal: His grandson Congxin, in the Shenlong era, because his son Sou married a daughter of Princess Taiping, was repeatedly promoted to Palace Supervisor.
translations.idiomatic: His grandson Congxin rose during Shenlong, when his son Sou married a daughter of Princess Taiping, to repeated promotion as palace supervisor.

sentences.zh: 脧太常少卿，坐太平黨誅。

translations.literal: Sou was Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and was executed for belonging to the Princess Taiping faction.
translations.idiomatic: Sou, vice director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, was executed as a partisan of Princess Taiping.

sentences.zh: 儉弟憲。

translations.literal: Jian's younger brother Xian.
translations.idiomatic: Jian's younger brother was Xian.

sentences.zh: 憲字茂彜，仕隋爲東宮左勛衛。

translations.literal: Xian, style name Maoyi, served the Sui as Left Merit Guard of the Eastern Palace.
translations.idiomatic: Xian, style Maoyi, served the Sui as a left merit guard in the eastern palace.

sentences.zh: 太子廢，罷歸。

translations.literal: When the crown prince was deposed, he was dismissed and returned home.
translations.idiomatic: When the crown prince was deposed, he was dismissed and went home.

sentences.zh: 不治細行，好馳獵，藏亡命，所交皆博徒輕俠。

translations.literal: He did not govern small conduct, loved galloping in the hunt, harbored fugitives, and those he associated with were all gamblers and light swordsmen.
translations.idiomatic: He cared little for propriety, loved the chase, sheltered fugitives, and kept company with gamblers and swaggering swordsmen.

sentences.zh: 高祖領太原，頗親遇之，參與大議。

translations.literal: When Gaozu held Taiyuan, he was quite personally favored and took part in great deliberations.
translations.idiomatic: When Gaozu held Taiyuan he favored Xian personally and drew him into the great councils.

sentences.zh: 義師起，授正議大夫，置左右，尤所信倚。

translations.literal: When the righteous army rose, he was appointed Rectifier Grand Master, placed at left and right, and was especially trusted and relied upon.
translations.idiomatic: When the righteous army rose he was made rectifier grand master, kept at the ruler's side, and especially trusted.

sentences.zh: 封安富縣公。

translations.literal: He was enfeoffed as Duke of Anfu County.
translations.idiomatic: He was enfeoffed as Duke of Anfu.

sentences.zh: 武德中，進累雲麾將軍，加郡公。

translations.literal: In Wude he was advanced through ranks to Cloud-Banner General and given the additional title of Commandery Duke.
translations.idiomatic: During Wude he rose to cloud-banner general and received the additional title of commandery duke.

sentences.zh: 貞觀中，終金紫光祿大夫。

translations.literal: In Zhenguan he ended as Grand Master of Splendid Gold and Purple.
translations.idiomatic: Under Zhenguan he ended his career as grand master of splendid gold and purple.

sentences.zh: 儉裔孫 次裔孫次，字文編。

translations.literal: Jian's descendant-grandson Ci: Ci, style name Wenbian.
translations.idiomatic: A descendant of Jian's line, Ci, style Wenbian.

sentences.zh: 建中初，及進士第，歷侍御史。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Jianzhong he passed the Presented Scholar examination and served as Attending Censor.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Jianzhong he passed the presented scholar examination and served as attending censor.

sentences.zh: 竇參數薦之，改禮部員外郎。

translations.literal: Dou Can repeatedly recommended him; he was transferred to Ministry of Rites Vice Director.
translations.idiomatic: Dou Can repeatedly recommended him, and he became vice director in the Ministry of Rites.

sentences.zh: 參貶，出爲開州刺史，積十年不遷。

translations.literal: When Can was demoted, Ci went out as Prefect of Kaizhou and for ten accumulated years received no transfer.
translations.idiomatic: When Can fell, Ci was sent out as prefect of Kaizhou and went ten years without promotion.

sentences.zh: 韋臯鎮蜀，表爲副使，德宗諭臯罷之。

translations.literal: Wei Gao governed Shu and memorialized him as deputy commissioner; Dezong instructed Gao to withdraw it.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Gao, governing Shu, recommended him as deputy commissioner, but Dezong ordered Gao to withdraw the nomination.

sentences.zh: 次身在遠，久抑不得申，以爲古忠臣賢士罹讒毀被放，至殺身，君且不悟者，因采獲其事，爲《辯謗略》三篇上之。

translations.literal: Ci, body in the distant regions, long suppressed and unable to express himself, believed that ancient loyal ministers and worthy gentlemen who suffered slander and banishment, even to death, while rulers did not awaken—therefore he gathered such cases and made three fascicles of Outline for Refuting Slander, which he submitted.
translations.idiomatic: Far from court and long unable to speak, Ci believed that loyal ministers of old had been slandered, exiled, and even killed while their rulers never understood. He collected such cases in three fascicles called Outline for Refuting Slander and submitted them.

sentences.zh: 帝益怒，曰：「是乃以古昏主方我！」

translations.literal: The emperor grew still angrier and said: "This is using ancient benighted rulers to compare with me!"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor grew angrier still and said, "You compare me to benighted rulers of old!"

sentences.zh: 改夔州刺史。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Prefect of Qizhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to prefect of Qizhou.

sentences.zh: 憲宗立，召還，授禮部郎中，知制誥，終中書舍人。

translations.literal: When Xianzong acceded, he was summoned back, appointed Ministry of Rites Director, charged with drafting edicts, and ended as Secretariat Drafter.
translations.idiomatic: When Xianzong came to the throne Ci was recalled, made director in the Ministry of Rites and drafter of edicts, and ended as secretariat drafter.

sentences.zh: 憲宗雅惡朋比傾陷者，嘗覽《辯謗略》，善之。

translations.literal: Xianzong by nature detested factional plotting and frame-ups; he once perused the Outline for Refuting Slander and approved it.
translations.idiomatic: Xianzong detested cliques and framed accusations; when he read the Outline for Refuting Slander he approved it.

sentences.zh: 謂學士沈傳師曰：「凡君人者，宜所觀省。

translations.literal: He said to Academician Shen Chuanshi: "Every ruler ought to examine this.
translations.idiomatic: He told academician Shen Chuanshi, "Every ruler ought to read this.

sentences.zh: 然次編錄未盡，卿可廣其書。」

translations.literal: Yet Ci's compilation is not complete—you may expand the book."
translations.idiomatic: But Ci's compilation is incomplete—you should expand the work."

sentences.zh: 傳師乃與令狐楚、杜元穎論次，起周訖隋，增爲十篇，更號《元和辨謗略》。

translations.literal: Chuanshi then, with Linghu Chu and Du Yuanying, arranged the material from Zhou through Sui, increased it to ten fascicles, and retitled it Outline for Refuting Slander of the Yuanhe Era.
translations.idiomatic: Chuanshi, with Linghu Chu and Du Yuanying, arranged cases from Zhou through Sui, expanded the work to ten fascicles, and retitled it the Yuanhe Outline for Refuting Slander.

sentences.zh: 次子 扶子扶，字雲翔，仕歷屯田郎中。

translations.literal: The second son Fu: Fu, style name Yunxiang, in office rose to Director of State Farms.
translations.idiomatic: Ci's second son Fu, style Yunxiang, rose to director of state farms.

sentences.zh: 大和五年，爲山南宣撫使。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Dahe he was Pacification Commissioner of Shannan.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of Dahe he served as pacification commissioner of Shannan.

sentences.zh: 內鄉倉督鄧琬負度支漕米七千斛，吏責償之，系其父子至孫凡二十八年，九人死於獄，扶奏申釋之。

translations.literal: Deng Wan, granary overseer of Neixiang, owed seven thousand hu of transport grain to the Revenue Ministry; officials demanded repayment and imprisoned father, son, and grandson for twenty-eight years in all; nine people died in prison. Fu memorialized to report and secure release.
translations.idiomatic: Deng Wan, granary overseer at Neixiang, owed seven thousand hu of transport grain to the Revenue Ministry. Officials demanded repayment and imprisoned his family for twenty-eight years; nine died in prison. Fu memorialized for their release.

sentences.zh: 詔切責鹽鐵、度支二使，天下監院償逋系三年以上者，皆原。

translations.literal: An edict sharply rebuked the two commissioners of Salt-Iron and Revenue; throughout the realm, those in supervisory depots imprisoned for debt repayment for three years or more were all pardoned.
translations.idiomatic: An edict sharply rebuked the salt-iron and revenue commissioners and pardoned everyone in the empire imprisoned three years or more for depot debts.

sentences.zh: 進中書舍人，出爲福州觀察使。

translations.literal: He was advanced to Secretariat Drafter and went out as Observation Commissioner of Fuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to secretariat drafter and sent out as observation commissioner of Fuzhou.

sentences.zh: 濫殺人，風績不立。

translations.literal: He killed people indiscriminately and established no reputation for conduct.
translations.idiomatic: He killed indiscriminately and won no reputation for good governance.

sentences.zh: 會卒，奴婢爭財，有司按其貲至十餘萬，時議蚩薄之。

translations.literal: When he happened to die, slave women and servants fought over property; the authorities inventoried his wealth to more than a hundred thousand, and opinion of the time despised him.
translations.idiomatic: He soon died; his servants fought over his estate, and officials found more than a hundred thousand in assets. Public opinion despised him.

sentences.zh: 次子 持扶弟持，字德守，中進士第。

translations.literal: The second son Chi, Fu's younger brother Chi, style name Deshou, passed the Presented Scholar examination.
translations.idiomatic: Fu's younger brother Chi, style Deshou, passed the presented scholar examination.

sentences.zh: 大和中，爲渭南尉，試京兆府進士。

translations.literal: In Dahe he was Magistrate of Weinan and examined Presented Scholars for the Jingzhao Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: During Dahe he was magistrate of Weinan and examiner of presented scholars for Jingzhao.

sentences.zh: 時尹杜悰欲以親故託之，持輒趨降階伏，悰語塞，乃止。

translations.literal: At the time Intendant Du Cong wished to entrust a relative through him; Chi at once hurried down the steps and prostrated himself. Cong was speechless and stopped.
translations.idiomatic: The intendant Du Cong tried to secure favor for a kinsman through him; Chi hurried down the steps and prostrated himself. Cong fell silent and desisted.

sentences.zh: 累遷工部郎中，出爲容州刺史。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly transferred to Works Ministry Director and went out as Prefect of Rongzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to director in the Ministry of Works and was sent out as prefect of Rongzhou.

sentences.zh: 遷給事中，歷朔方、昭義節度使，卒。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Drafting Attendant Within, served as Military Governor of Shuofang and Zhaoyi, and died.
translations.idiomatic: He became drafting attendant within, served as military governor of Shuofang and Zhaoyi, and died.

sentences.zh: 持子 彥謙子彥謙字茂業，多通技藝，尤工爲詩，負才無所屈。

translations.literal: Chi's son Yanqian: Yanqian, style name Maoye, was broadly skilled in arts and especially adept at poetry; bearing talent, he bowed to none.
translations.idiomatic: Chi's son Yanqian, style Maoye, mastered many arts and especially poetry; proud of his talent, he bowed to no one.

sentences.zh: 乾符末，避亂漢南。

translations.literal: At the end of Qianfu he avoided turmoil in Hannan.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of Qianfu he fled the turmoil to Hannan.

sentences.zh: 王重榮鎮河中，辟幕府，累表爲副，歷晉、絳二州刺史。

translations.literal: Wang Chongrong governed Hezhong and recruited him to the staff office; he was repeatedly memorialized as deputy and served as Prefect of Jin and Jiang prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Chongrong, governing Hezhong, took him onto his staff, repeatedly recommended him as deputy, and had him serve as prefect of Jin and Jiang.

sentences.zh: 重榮軍亂、彥謙貶興元參軍事。

translations.literal: When Chongrong's army mutinied, Yanqian was demoted to Staff Officer of Xingyuan.
translations.idiomatic: After Chongrong's mutiny, Yanqian was demoted to staff officer at Xingyuan.

sentences.zh: 節度使楊守亮表爲判官，遷副使，終閬、壁二州刺史。

translations.literal: Military Governor Yang Shouliang memorialized him as administrative aide; he was transferred to deputy commissioner and ended as Prefect of Lang and Bi prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Shouliang, military governor, recommended him as aide, then deputy commissioner; he ended as prefect of Lang and Bi.

sentences.zh: 段志玄，齊州臨淄人。

translations.literal: Duan Zhixuan, a man of Linzi in Qizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Duan Zhixuan was a native of Linzi in Qizhou.

sentences.zh: 父偃師，仕隋爲太原司法書佐。

translations.literal: His father Yanshi served the Sui as Judicial Clerk of Taiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: His father Yanshi served the Sui as judicial clerk at Taiyuan.

sentences.zh: 從義師，官至郢州刺史。

translations.literal: He followed the righteous army and rose to Prefect of Yingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He followed the righteous army and rose to prefect of Yingzhou.

sentences.zh: 志玄姿質偉岸，少無賴，數犯法。

translations.literal: Zhixuan's bearing was grand and imposing; in youth he was a scoundrel and repeatedly broke the law.
translations.idiomatic: Zhixuan was tall and imposing; in youth he was a scoundrel who repeatedly ran afoul of the law.

sentences.zh: 大業末，從父客太原，以票果，諸惡少年畏之，爲秦王所識。

translations.literal: At the end of Daye he followed his father as a guest in Taiyuan; for swift daring, all the vicious youths feared him, and he was noticed by the Prince of Qin.
translations.idiomatic: Late in Daye he followed his father to Taiyuan. His daring made the local rowdies fear him, and the Prince of Qin took notice.

sentences.zh: 高祖興，以千人從，授右領大都督府軍頭。

translations.literal: When Gaozu rose, he followed with a thousand men and was appointed Army Head of the Right Leading Grand Commander's Office.
translations.idiomatic: When Gaozu rose, Zhixuan followed with a thousand men and was made army head in the right leading grand commander's office.

sentences.zh: 下霍邑、絳郡，攻永豐倉，椎鋒最。

translations.literal: He took Huoyi and Jiang Commandery, attacked the Yongfeng granary, and was foremost in the assault wedge.
translations.idiomatic: He helped take Huoyi and Jiang commandery, stormed the Yongfeng granary, and led the assault wedge.

sentences.zh: 歷左光祿大夫。

translations.literal: He served as Left Grand Master for Splendid Happiness.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to left grand master for splendid happiness.

sentences.zh: 從劉文靜拒屈突通於潼關。

translations.literal: He followed Liu Wenjing in resisting Qu Tuntong at Tong Pass.
translations.idiomatic: He followed Liu Wenjing in holding Tong Pass against Qu Tuntong.

sentences.zh: 文靜爲桑顯和所襲，軍且潰，志玄率壯騎馳賊，殺十餘人，中流矢，忍不言，突擊自如，賊眾亂，軍乘之，唐兵復振。

translations.literal: Wenjing was struck by Sang Xianhe; the army was about to collapse. Zhixuan led stalwart cavalry to charge the enemy, killed more than ten men, was struck by a flowing arrow yet endured without speaking, and pressed the assault as before. The enemy masses fell into disorder; the army seized the moment and Tang troops rallied again.
translations.idiomatic: When Sang Xianhe routed Wenjing and the army nearly broke, Zhixuan led picked horsemen into the enemy, killed more than ten men, took an arrow and said nothing, and kept charging. The rebels fell into disorder; the Tang line rallied.

sentences.zh: 通敗走，與諸將躡獲於稠桑，以多，授樂遊府車騎將軍。

translations.literal: Tuntong was defeated and fled; with the generals they pursued and captured him at Chousang. For great merit he was appointed Cavalry General of the Leyou Office.
translations.idiomatic: Tuntong fled and was captured at Chousang. For his merit Zhixuan was made cavalry general of the Leyou office.

sentences.zh: 從討王世充，深入，馬跌，爲賊禽。

translations.literal: Following the campaign against Wang Shichong, he went deep in; his horse fell and he was seized by bandits.
translations.idiomatic: In the campaign against Wang Shichong he pushed deep, his horse fell, and the enemy seized him.

sentences.zh: 兩騎夾持其髻，將度洛，志玄忽騰而上，二人者俱墮，於是奪其馬馳歸，尾騎數百不敢近。

translations.literal: Two horsemen gripped his topknot, about to cross the Luo; Zhixuan suddenly vaulted upward, and both men fell together. He then seized their horse and galloped back; several hundred pursuers dared not approach.
translations.idiomatic: Two riders gripped his topknot to drag him across the Luo. Zhixuan surged upward and threw them both down, seized a horse, and galloped back while hundreds of pursuers dared not close.

sentences.zh: 破竇建德，平東都，遷秦王府右二護軍。

translations.literal: He broke Dou Jiande, pacified the Eastern Capital, and was transferred to Second Protector of the Prince of Qin's Right Wing.
translations.idiomatic: He helped defeat Dou Jiande and pacify the eastern capital, then became second protector of the Prince of Qin's right wing.

sentences.zh: 隱太子嘗以金帛誘之，拒不納。

translations.literal: The Hidden Crown Prince once tried to entice him with gold and silks; he refused and would not accept.
translations.idiomatic: The Hidden Crown Prince once tried to buy him with gold and silk; he refused.

sentences.zh: 秦王即位，累遷左驍衛大將軍，封樊國公，實封九百戸。

translations.literal: When the Prince of Qin acceded, he was repeatedly transferred to Left Brave Guard General-in-Chief, enfeoffed as Duke of Fan, with a substantive fief of nine hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: When the prince became emperor, Zhixuan rose to left brave guard general-in-chief, was enfeoffed as Duke of Fan, and received a substantive fief of nine hundred households.

sentences.zh: 詔率兵至青海奪吐谷渾牧馬，逗留，免。

translations.literal: An edict ordered him to lead troops to Qinghai to seize Tuyuhun pasture horses; he lingered and was dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: Ordered to lead troops to Qinghai to seize Tuyuhun horses, he lingered and was dismissed.

sentences.zh: 未幾復職。

translations.literal: Before long he was restored to office.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon restored to office.

sentences.zh: 文德皇后之葬，與宇文士及勒兵衛章武門，太宗夜遣使至二將軍所，士及披戸內使，志玄拒曰：「軍門不夜開。」

translations.literal: At the burial of Empress Wende, he and Yuwen Shiji drew up troops to guard Zhangwu Gate. Taizong at night sent an envoy to the two generals' posts; Shiji pushed open the door and admitted the envoy. Zhixuan refused, saying: "The army gate is not opened at night."
translations.idiomatic: At Empress Wende's burial he and Yuwen Shiji guarded Zhangwu Gate. Taizong sent a night envoy; Shiji opened the gate, but Zhixuan refused, saying, "Army gates do not open at night."

sentences.zh: 使者示手詔，志玄曰：「夜不能辨。」

translations.literal: The envoy showed the handwritten edict; Zhixuan said: "At night one cannot distinguish."
translations.idiomatic: The envoy showed the emperor's handwritten order. Zhixuan said, "One cannot verify orders in the dark."

sentences.zh: 不納。

translations.literal: He would not admit them.
translations.idiomatic: He would not admit them.

sentences.zh: 比曙，帝嘆曰：「真將軍，周亞夫何以加！」

translations.literal: By dawn the emperor sighed and said: "A true general—how could Zhou Yafu surpass this!"
translations.idiomatic: At dawn the emperor sighed, "A true general—how could even Zhou Yafu do better!"

sentences.zh: 改封褒國公，歷鎮軍大將軍。

translations.literal: His title was changed to Duke of Bao, and he served as Suppressing-Army Grand General.
translations.idiomatic: His title was changed to Duke of Bao and he became suppressing-army grand general.

sentences.zh: 貞觀十六年疾，帝臨視，泣顧曰：「當與卿子五品官。」

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year of Zhenguan he fell ill; the emperor visited him in person, wept, and turning said: "I shall give your son a fifth-rank office."
translations.idiomatic: In the sixteenth year of Zhenguan he fell ill. The emperor visited him, wept, and said, "I will give your son a fifth-rank post."

sentences.zh: 頓首謝，請與母弟，乃拜志感左衛郎將。

translations.literal: He bowed his head in thanks and requested it for his younger brother by the same mother; thereupon Zhigan was appointed Left Guard Commandant.
translations.idiomatic: He kowtowed in thanks and asked that the favor go to his younger brother instead; Zhigan was appointed left guard commandant.

sentences.zh: 及卒，帝哭之慟。

translations.literal: When he died, the emperor wept for him in deep grief.
translations.idiomatic: When he died the emperor wept bitterly.

sentences.zh: 贈輔國大將軍、揚州都督，陪葬昭陵，謚曰壯肅。

translations.literal: Posthumously conferred Assisting-State Grand General and Regional Inspector of Yangzhou; buried with honor at Zhaoling; posthumous title Zhuangsu.
translations.idiomatic: The court posthumously made him assisting-state grand general and regional inspector of Yangzhou, buried him beside Zhaoling, and gave him the posthumous name Zhuangsu.

sentences.zh: 三世孫文昌。

translations.literal: His third-generation descendant was Wenchang.
translations.idiomatic: His third-generation descendant was Wenchang.

sentences.zh: 志玄三世孫 文昌文昌，字墨卿，一字景初，世客荊州。

translations.literal: Zhixuan's third-generation descendant Wenchang: Wenchang, style name Moqing, also styled Jingchu, for generations a sojourner in Jingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Zhixuan's third-generation descendant Wenchang, also styled Jingchu, came from a family long settled in Jingzhou.

sentences.zh: 疏爽任義節，不爲齷齪小行。

translations.literal: Open and bold, he trusted righteousness and integrity and would not perform petty, sordid acts.
translations.idiomatic: Open and bold, he lived by righteousness and scorned petty conduct.

sentences.zh: 節度使裴胄禮之。

translations.literal: Military Governor Pei Zhou honored him.
translations.idiomatic: The military governor Pei Zhou treated him with honor.

sentences.zh: 胄采古今禮要爲書，數從文昌質判所疑。

translations.literal: Zhou gathered ancient and modern ritual essentials into a book and repeatedly sought Wenchang to judge and decide what was doubtful.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou compiled a book of ritual essentials and often asked Wenchang to resolve his doubts.

sentences.zh: 後依劍南節度韋臯，臯表爲校書郎。

translations.literal: Later he relied on Jiannan Military Governor Wei Gao; Gao memorialized him as Collator.
translations.idiomatic: He later entered the service of Wei Gao, military governor of Jiannan, who recommended him as collator.

sentences.zh: 宰相李吉甫才之，擢登封尉、集賢校理，再遷左補闕。

translations.literal: Chief Minister Li Jifu recognized his talent and promoted him to Magistrate of Dengfeng and Collation Corrector of the Hall of Worthies, then again transferred to Left Remonstrator.
translations.idiomatic: Chief minister Li Jifu recognized his talent, made him magistrate of Dengfeng and collation corrector in the Hall of Worthies, then left remonstrator.

sentences.zh: 憲宗數欲親用，頗爲韋貫之奇詆，偃蹇不得進。

translations.literal: Xianzong several times wished to employ him personally, but he was rather subject to Wei Guanzhi's strange slanders and, stalled, could not advance.
translations.idiomatic: Xianzong several times wished to promote him personally, but Wei Guanzhi's odd attacks blocked his advance.

sentences.zh: 貫之罷，引爲翰林學士，遷中書舍人，遂爲承旨。

translations.literal: When Guanzhi was dismissed, he was brought in as Hanlin Academician, transferred to Secretariat Drafter, and then became Drafting Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: After Guanzhi's dismissal he entered the Hanlin Academy, became secretariat drafter, and then drafting commissioner.

sentences.zh: 穆宗即位，屢召入思政殿顧問，率至夕乃出。

translations.literal: When Muzong acceded, he was repeatedly summoned into the Hall of Governance and Thought for consultation, usually not leaving until evening.
translations.idiomatic: When Muzong came to the throne he was repeatedly summoned to the Hall of Governance and Thought and usually stayed until evening.

sentences.zh: 俄拜中書侍郎、同中書門下平章事。

translations.literal: Soon he was appointed Secretariat Vice Director and Associate of the Secretariat-Chancellery with the Peaceful Administration Seal.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon made secretariat vice director and associate chief councilor.

sentences.zh: 未逾年，自表還政。

translations.literal: Before a year had passed, he himself memorialized to return power.
translations.idiomatic: Within a year he memorialized to resign from the council.

sentences.zh: 授劍南西川節度使、同平章事。

translations.literal: He was appointed Military Governor of Jiannan West Circuit and Associate Chief Councilor.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed military governor of Jiannan West circuit with the title of associate chief councilor.

sentences.zh: 文昌素諳蜀利病，大抵治寬靜，間以威斷，不常任也，群蠻震服。

translations.literal: Wenchang was by nature well versed in Shu profit and harm; broadly he governed with lenience and calm, interspersed with stern decisiveness, not relying on routine measures, and the tribal peoples were awed into submission.
translations.idiomatic: Wenchang knew Shu well. He governed mostly with lenience and calm, punctuated by stern decisiveness rather than routine harshness, and the tribes submitted in awe.

sentences.zh: 長慶二年黔中蠻叛，觀察使崔元略以聞，文昌使一介開曉，蠻即引還，彭濮蠻大酋蹉祿來請立石刊誓，脩貢獻。

translations.literal: In the second year of Changqing the Qianzhong tribes rebelled; Observation Commissioner Cui Yuanlue reported it. Wenchang sent a single envoy to enlighten them, and the tribes at once withdrew. Cuolu, great chieftain of the Peng-Pu tribes, came to request erecting stone and carving an oath, and restored tribute offerings.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Changqing the Qianzhong tribes rebelled. Wenchang sent one envoy to reason with them and they withdrew. Cuolu, chieftain of the Peng-Pu tribes, asked to carve an oath in stone and restore tribute.

sentences.zh: 入遷兵部尚書。

translations.literal: He entered the capital and was transferred to Minister of War.
translations.idiomatic: Recalled to court, he became minister of war.

sentences.zh: 文宗立，拜御史大夫，進封鄒平郡公。

translations.literal: When Wenzong acceded, he was appointed Censor-in-Chief and advanced to Duke of Zouping Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: When Wenzong came to the throne he was made censor-in-chief and advanced to Duke of Zouping.

sentences.zh: 俄檢校尚書右僕射、平章事，節度淮南。

translations.literal: Soon he was Acting Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs and Chief Councilor, governing Huainan as Military Governor.
translations.idiomatic: He soon became acting right vice director and chief councilor while governing Huainan as military governor.

sentences.zh: 太和四年，檢校左僕射，徙帥荊南。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Taihe he was Acting Left Vice Director and transferred to command Jingnan.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Taihe he became acting left vice director and was transferred to command Jingnan.

sentences.zh: 州或旱，禬解必雨；

translations.literal: When the prefecture suffered drought, his prayer and exorcism always brought rain;
translations.idiomatic: When drought struck the prefecture, his prayers always brought rain;

sentences.zh: 或久雨，遇出遊必霽。

translations.literal: when rain lasted long, if he went out on tour it always cleared.
translations.idiomatic: when rain lingered, his outings always brought clear skies.

sentences.zh: 民爲語曰：「旱不苦，禱而雨；

translations.literal: The people made a saying: "Drought is not bitter—pray and rain comes;
translations.idiomatic: The people said, "Drought is no hardship—pray and rain comes;

sentences.zh: 雨不愁，公出遊。」

translations.literal: rain brings no worry—the lord goes out on tour."
translations.idiomatic: rain brings no worry—the lord goes touring."

sentences.zh: 南詔襲南安，帝以文昌得蠻夷心，詔使下檄尉讓，即日解而去。

translations.literal: Nanzhao raided Nan'an; the emperor, because Wenchang had won the hearts of the tribes, ordered an envoy to issue a placard of comfort and rebuke, and on the same day they withdrew and left.
translations.idiomatic: When Nanzhao attacked Nan'an, the emperor sent Wenchang—who had won the tribes' hearts—to issue a rebuking placard, and the raiders withdrew the same day.

sentences.zh: 復節度西川。

translations.literal: He again governed West Sichuan as Military Governor.
translations.idiomatic: He again governed West Sichuan.

sentences.zh: 九年卒，贈太尉。

translations.literal: In the ninth year he died; posthumously conferred Grand Preceptor.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the ninth year and was posthumously made grand preceptor.

sentences.zh: 文昌先墓在荊州，歲時享祠，必薦以音樂歌舞，習禮者譏其非，少羈窶，所向少諧。

translations.literal: Wenchang's ancestral tomb was in Jingzhou; at seasonal sacrifices he always offered music and song-dance. Those versed in ritual mocked this as improper. In youth he was constrained and poor; wherever he went he rarely found harmony.
translations.idiomatic: His ancestral tomb lay in Jingzhou, where he offered music and dance at the seasonal rites—conduct ritualists mocked. Poor in youth, he rarely found favor wherever he went.

sentences.zh: 及居將相，享用奢侈，士議尤替。

translations.literal: When he reached the rank of general and minister, his enjoyment was extravagant, and opinion among gentlemen especially despised him.
translations.idiomatic: Once he reached the highest offices his life turned extravagant, and gentlemen despised him all the more.

sentences.zh: 文昌子 成式子成式，字柯古，推廕爲校書郎。

translations.literal: Wenchang's son Chengshi: Chengshi, style name Kegu, entered office by yin privilege as Collator.
translations.idiomatic: Wenchang's son Chengshi, style Kegu, entered office by yin privilege as collator.

sentences.zh: 博學強記，多奇篇秘籍。

translations.literal: Broadly learned with a powerful memory, he possessed many strange works and secret texts.
translations.idiomatic: Learned and with a formidable memory, he collected rare and secret texts.

sentences.zh: 侍父於蜀，以畋獵自放，文昌遣吏自其意諫止。

translations.literal: Attending his father in Shu, he gave himself to hunting; Wenchang sent an official to admonish him in his own manner and stop him.
translations.idiomatic: While attending his father in Shu he gave himself to the hunt. Wenchang sent an official to dissuade him in his own way.

sentences.zh: 明日以雉兔遍遺幕府，人爲書，因所獲儷前世事，無復用者，眾大驚。

translations.literal: The next day he sent pheasants and hares throughout the staff offices; men composed writings, pairing by his catch events of former ages with no further use—everyone was greatly astonished.
translations.idiomatic: The next day he sent pheasants and hares to every office in the staff. His companions wrote pieces pairing each animal with historical precedents until no precedent remained unused. All were astonished.

sentences.zh: 擢累尚書郎，爲吉州刺史，終太常少卿。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to Department of State Affairs Attendant, served as Prefect of Jizhou, and ended as Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through posts in the Department of State Affairs, served as prefect of Jizhou, and ended as vice director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 著《酉陽書》數十篇。

translations.literal: He authored several tens of fascicles of the Book of Youyang.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote several tens of fascicles of the Book of Youyang.

sentences.zh: 子安節，乾寧中，爲國子司業。

translations.literal: His son Anjie, in Qianning, was Vice-Director of the Directorate of Education.
translations.idiomatic: His son Anjie served during Qianning as vice-director of the Directorate of Education.

sentences.zh: 善樂律，能自度曲云。

translations.literal: He was skilled in musical pitch and law and could himself compose tunes, it is said.
translations.idiomatic: He was skilled in music theory and, it is said, could compose tunes himself.

sentences.zh: 贊贊曰：屈突通盡節於隋，而爲唐忠臣，何哉？

translations.literal: Commentary: Commentary says: Qu Tuntong fulfilled integrity under the Sui yet became a Tang loyal minister—how so?
translations.idiomatic: Commentary: Qu Tuntong kept faith with the Sui yet became a loyal minister of Tang—how can that be?

sentences.zh: 惟其一心，故事兩君而無嫌也。

translations.literal: Only because his heart was one could he serve two rulers without suspicion.
translations.idiomatic: Because his heart was single, he could serve two rulers without reproach.

sentences.zh: 敬德之來，太宗以赤心付之，桑廕不徙而大功立。

translations.literal: When Jingde came, Taizong entrusted him with a red heart; the mulberry shade did not shift yet great merit was established.
translations.idiomatic: When Jingde came, Taizong entrusted him with his whole heart; like a tree whose shade never moves, great deeds were accomplished.

sentences.zh: 君臣相遇，古人謂之千載，顧不諒哉！

translations.literal: Such a meeting of ruler and minister the ancients called once in a thousand years—how could it not be understood!
translations.idiomatic: Such a meeting of ruler and minister the ancients called once in a thousand years—can it not be understood?

sentences.zh: 投幾之會，間不容穟，公謹所以抵龜而決也。

translations.literal: The moment of casting the stalks allows no grain of slack; therefore Gongjin struck the tortoise and decided.
translations.idiomatic: At the turning point of fate not a grain of slack is allowed—hence Gongjin struck the tortoise and chose.
